Banner Health believes leadership matters. We look for leaders who share our vision making health care easier, so life can be better. Our executives are at the forefront of the health care transformation, planning the future of Banner Health.


This leadership role is responsible for shaping and executing the organization's cybersecurity engineering strategy, with a strong focus on Zero Trust architecture, network security, identity and access management, cloud security, and data protection. The position partners closely with executive leadership to drive transformational security initiatives, align cybersecurity investments with business objectives, and establish a roadmap for security maturity across the enterprise.

Your pay and benefits are important components of your journey at Banner Health. This opportunity includes the option to participate in a variety of health, financial, and security benefits. In addition, this position may be eligible for our Management Incentive Program as part of your Total Rewards package.Within Banner Health Corporate, you will have the opportunity to apply your unique experience and expertise in support of a nationally-recognized healthcare leader. We offer stimulating and rewarding careers in a wide array of disciplines. Whether your background is in Human Resources, Finance, Information Technology, Legal, Managed Care Programs or Public Relations, you'll find many options for contributing to our award-winning patient care.

POSITION SUMMARY

This position leads the strategic development, implementation, and ongoing management of the organization's cybersecurity engineering framework. This role drives transformational security initiatives across network infrastructure, identity and access management, data protection, and configuration management domains. This position includes influencing the vision and strategy of Banner’s cybersecurity, staying current on the latest technology trends, understanding market changes and business needs, and working with senior leadership to develop and drive the direction. Partners and collaborates with other security and IT leaders to develop and drive strategies, work on special projects, and solve complex security challenges facing the organization.


CORE FUNCTIONS

1. Develops and executes comprehensive zero trust strategy aligned with organizational business objectives and risk tolerance. Establishes roadmap for zero trust maturity progression across all security domains. Provides executive leadership on security architecture decisions and investments. Collaborates with C-suite and business unit leaders to integrate zero trust principles into digital transformation initiatives. Defines success metrics and KPIs for zero trust implementation and effectiveness. Supports and promotes security governance and ensures security architectures are aligned to business priority, comply with reference architecture standards, policy and regulatory requirements. Ensures Key Performance Indicators are established and tracked in all levels of work effort.


2. Designs and implements micro-segmentation strategies to minimize lateral movement and contain potential breaches. Leads deployment and optimization of Zscaler cloud security platform for secure internet and SaaS access. Architects zero trust network access (ZTNA) solutions replacing traditional VPN infrastructure. Oversees network security policies, enforcement mechanisms, and continuous monitoring. Ensures secure connectivity for remote workforce, partners, and third-party access.


3. Establishes identity-centric security controls as the foundation of zero trust architecture. Implements adaptive authentication, multi-factor authentication (MFA), and risk-based access policies. Leads privileged access management (PAM) and just-in-time (JIT) access initiatives. Drives identity governance programs including access certification and lifecycle management. Integrates IAM with SIEM/SOAR platforms for threat detection and automated response.


4. Develops data classification framework and implements appropriate protection controls. Deploys data loss prevention (DLP), encryption, and rights management solutions. Establishes data access policies based on least privilege and need-to-know principles. Implements cloud access security broker (CASB) technologies for SaaS data protection. Ensures compliance with data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, etc.).


5. Establishes security configuration baselines and hardening standards across all technology platforms. Implements infrastructure as code (IaC) with embedded security controls. Leads vulnerability management and patch management programs. Deploys configuration monitoring and drift detection capabilities. Ensures secure DevSecOps practices and CI/CD pipeline security.


6. Builds, mentors, and leads high-performing security engineering and architecture teams in a fully remote environment. Fosters culture of continuous learning and security innovation. Develops talent pipeline and succession planning for critical security roles. Collaborates with HR on security awareness training and culture initiatives. Creates inclusive remote work culture with strong team cohesion across distributed workforce.


7. Ensures zero trust implementation meets regulatory and compliance requirements. Establishes security policies, standards, and procedures aligned with industry frameworks (NIST, ISO 27001). Coordinates with audit, risk, and compliance teams on security assessments. Manages vendor relationships and third-party security assessments.


8. Analyzes business and IT security environment to detect critical deficiencies and/or redundancies and recommends solutions for improvement. Documents current state security architecture, integrates new security solutions into existing systems and deploys solutions that meet emerging business security needs.


9. Serves as a credible expert advisor to peers and senior and executive leadership on the appropriateness of current and future security technologies based on the highest level of Total Cost of Ownership, Return on Investment, and strategic value to the business.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS


Requires Master's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Security, Information Systems, Computer Science, or related field, or equivalent of education and work experience.


Requires ten years of current and progressive experience in information security and cybersecurity leadership, including five plus years in senior leadership roles managing enterprise security programs.


Requires proven track record implementing protective technology in complex enterprise environments. Requires extensive hands-on experience with Zscaler or similar cloud security platforms. Requires deep expertise in network segmentation, microsegmentation, and software-defined perimeter technologies. Requires strong background in IAM platforms (Okta, Azure AD, Ping Identity, SailPoint, CyberArk). Requires experience with data security technologies (DLP, CASB, encryption, tokenization). Requires demonstrated success with configuration management and infrastructure as code tools.


Requires proven ability to lead and manage distributed remote teams effectively.


Requires expert knowledge of zero trust principles and frameworks (NIST SP 800-207, Forrester, Gartner). Requires advanced understanding of network protocols, architectures, and security controls. Requires proficiency with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) and cloud-native security. Requires strong knowledge of identity protocols (SAML, OAuth, OIDC, Kerberos, LDAP). Requires familiarity with SIEM, SOAR, EDR, and security analytics platforms. Requires understanding of DevSecOps practices and security automation.


Requires proficient understanding of regulatory and compliance mandates, including but not limited to HIPAA, HITECH, PCI, Sarbanes-Oxley, GDPR, CCPA, and knowledge of compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, CIS Controls).


Requires technical project experience designing, developing, integrating, and implementing solutions to resolve complex technical and business issues.


This position may require off-site travel for annual team gatherings, conferences, or critical vendor meetings.


As is typical in this industry, variable shifts or on-call hours and responding to off-hour paging may be required. This position requires on-call availability for security incidents and escalations.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS


CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional)

CISM (Certified Information Security Manager)

CCSP (Certified Cloud Security Professional)

CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor)

Vendor-specific certifications (Zscaler, cloud platforms, IAM solutions)


Additional related education and/or experience preferred.

Remote option is available for this position.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your excellence in an inclusive, collaborative, and empowering community? Are you excited about joining a company that strives to make a difference – for its employees, clients, and society? Are you motivated by creating sustainable change that benefits society and nature?

If this sounds like you, or you’re curious to learn more, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our Workplace Management team and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

Your new role

This role provides senior HSE leadership across Ramboll’s EPC/EPCM project portfolio in Ramboll Americas, supporting the safe delivery of complex engineering, procurement, construction management, commissioning, and turnover activities. The role is responsible for establishing consistent HSE governance, aligning contractors and project teams, supporting high-risk work planning, and enabling effective execution across multiple concurrent projects. The successful candidate will bring significant hands-on experience from large-scale EPC/EPCM construction environments and will be able to operate confidently at both strategic and field execution levels.

The ideal candidate will be a credible HSE leader with significant field experience on large-scale construction or EPC/EPCM projects, strong contractor management capability, and the confidence to influence senior project, client, and contractor stakeholders. They will be comfortable working across multiple projects, balancing strategic governance with practical field-based support, and helping project teams create consistent, risk-based HSE execution.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Strategic HSE Leadership

  • Lead the development of a portfolio-wide HSE approach that enables consistent standards, scalable processes, and project-specific execution across all EPC/EPCM projects.
  • Serve as primary HSE advisor to Project Directors and EPC/EPCM leadership teams.
  • Drive adoption of Ramboll’s HSE program and translate its expectations into practical project-level behaviours, controls, and leadership routines.
  • Provide strategic HSE guidance during proposals and contract negotiations to align client expectations and establish the conditions needed for effective safety management.
  • Provide HSE leadership within an EPC/EPCM delivery model, ensuring clear boundaries, responsibilities, and interfaces between Ramboll, clients, construction contractors, subcontractors, and suppliers.

Safety Program Organization & Implementation

  • Define HSE organization structures that are scalable with the ability to support multi-project EPC/EPCM delivery on a nationwide basis.
  • Clarify roles, responsibilities, interfaces, and governance models required for integrated EPC/EPCM/ safety programs.
  • Establish standardized HSE execution plans across engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and turnover.
  • Establish construction readiness expectations, including contractor mobilisation, competency assurance, risk review, and field execution controls.

Contractor & Multi-Party Coordination

  • Align HSE expectations, execution standards, and performance requirements across contractors, subcontractors, vendors, and third-party stakeholders.
  • Lead contractor onboarding, alignment sessions, audits, and recurring performance reviews.
  • Ensure HSE requirements are embedded into contracting strategies, procurement packages, bid documents, mobilisation plans, and contractor management processes.
  • Support project teams in translating Ramboll and client HSE requirements into practical field execution requirements for contractors and subcontractors.

Risk Management, Governance and Assurance

  • Provide governance and assurance over EPC/EPCM risk management processes, including hazard identification, construction risk assessments, high-risk work reviews, and site controls.
  • Support project HSE resources and project leadership in establishing consistent risk management expectations, while ensuring accountability remains clear within the project delivery structure.
  • Review and challenge the effectiveness of controls for high-risk activities, including lifting, electrical work, confined space entry, work at height, ground disturbance, energisation, commissioning, and simultaneous operations.
  • Provide oversight, escalation support, and subject matter input for high-potential or higher-severity incidents, ensuring investigations are completed and lessons learned are embedded across relevant projects.
  • Conduct site visits, leadership engagements, and assurance reviews to verify that project HSE controls are effective, understood, and consistently applied by the relevant project teams and contractors.

Safety Culture & Engagement

  • Demonstrate visible HSE leadership that builds trust, accountability, and proactive safety behaviours across project teams and contractors.
  • Coach project and contractor leadership teams to strengthen leading indicators, reinforce expectations, and promote consistent safety leadership.
  • Promote open communication, psychological safety, learning, and continuous improvement across the EPC/EPCM project portfolio.

Regulatory & Compliance Oversight

  • Provide oversight of compliance with applicable health, safety, and environmental regulations, client requirements, and Ramboll HSE standards across EPC/EPCM projects.
  • Support project teams in translating regulatory and contractual HSE requirements into practical controls and assurance activities.
  • Represent Ramboll in client audits, regulatory inspections, and EPC/EPCM governance meetings, ensuring actions are effectively tracked, communicated, and closed.

Performance Management & Reporting

  • Establish consistent HSE performance reporting across EPC/EPCM projects, using leading and lagging indicators to identify trends, drive accountability, and improve performance.
  • Translate performance data into clear insights, actions, and recommendations for project leadership, clients, contractors, and internal stakeholders.

About you

  • Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Engineering, or related field.
  • 10+ years of progressive on-site HSE leadership experience with substantial large-scale EPC/EPCM project exposure.
  • Strong background supporting multi-contractor, high-risk industrial construction environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence without direct authority.
  • Proven experience supporting construction management delivery models where HSE performance is delivered through contractor execution and strong client/contractor interface management.
  • Working knowledge of construction-phase HSE controls, contractor management, incident investigation, assurance, and regulatory compliance.
  • Ability to travel regularly to project locations and engage effectively with field teams, project leadership, clients, and contractors.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred:

  • Professional certifications (CSP, CMIOSH, NEBOSH, CRSP, or equivalent).
  • Experience with energy transition, power, renewables, industrial de-carbonisation, chemicals, manufacturing, mining, or major infrastructure projects.
  • Experience supporting owner’s EPC/EPCM models across multiple concurrent projects.
  • International or remote project experience.

What we can offer you

  • Investment in your development
  • Being valued for the unique person you are
  • Never being short of inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects
  • The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $136,497 - $197,515 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

Ready to join us?

Please submit your application with your up-to-date CV. We invite diversity in all its forms and encourage applicants from all groups to apply.

Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in the Americas

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. About Engine

Engine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel. For a decade, Engine has built the proprietary technology and supply behind modern business travel, serving over 40,000 customers and nearly 2 million travelers, along with leading travel and AI companies that build on Engine's infrastructure. One system powers business travel, group travel, human agents, and AI agents.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

About the Role

Engine's Partner Growth team partners with a growing ecosystem of associations, fintech platforms, and distribution partners to bring Engine's free-to-use travel product to their members and customers. As Senior Partner Growth Manager, you will own the full lifecycle of Engine's most important channel relationships, from onboarding and enablement through deep performance optimization, driving revenue share growth across a portfolio that spans industries and partner types: associations, fintech and corporate spending platforms, marketplaces, and other distribution partners.

This is not a reactive account management role. You will function as a channel expert inside Engine's Partner Growth org, building the playbooks, relationships, and commercial frameworks that allow Engine to scale distribution through partners without sacrificing traveler experience or commercial performance. You'll sit at the intersection of partner acquisition and strategic account management, and you'll be expected to lead both internally and externally.

Why This Role Exists

Engine's channel partner network is entering a new phase of maturity. As the partner ecosystem grows and our largest relationships deepen, we need a dedicated owner who can enable partners to effectively position and distribute Engine to their audiences, and who understands the commercial levers that drive revenue share performance at scale. This hire is a critical seat on the channel team and is expected to immediately pick up a book of active relationships and drive them forward with minimal ramp time.

What You'll Own

Channel Partner Growth & Performance

  • Own end-to-end partner growth for a portfolio of channel partners spanning a range of industries, partner models, and scales
  • Drive GBV growth within existing channel partnerships through proactive commercial reviews, optimization initiatives, and joint go-to-market planning
  • Monitor partner health across production metrics, rate quality, and engagement, flagging risks and surfacing opportunities before they become problems
  • Ensure every partner in your portfolio has a regular cadence of meaningful touchpoints (no partner goes 60+ days without one), catching adoption or engagement gaps before they become churn risks
  • Lead QBRs and executive business reviews for strategic partners and structured health check-ins for the broader portfolio, translating data into forward-looking strategy rather than backward-looking reporting
  • Manage the commercial and contractual dimensions of partner relationships, including pricing discussions, tier reviews, and renewal negotiations
  • Serve as the first line of escalation for partner issues, coordinating internally with supply, product, and engineering to drive resolution
  • Own partner tier progression: actively move partners from Bronze toward Gold/Platinum status by unlocking the right milestones
  • Build multi-threaded relationships inside each partner across commercial, product, marketing, and operational contacts, so Engine's position doesn't depend on a single champion
  • Develop deep institutional knowledge of each partner's business model, product roadmap, and internal champions

Channel Ecosystem Development

  • Engage at contract signature to understand each partner's goals, stakeholders, and definition of success, then own the transition from the Partner Acquisition team to ongoing partner growth
  • Build and maintain channel-specific playbooks, onboarding frameworks, and partner enablement materials
  • Be the voice of the live partner base in internal product and roadmap discussions, translating partner needs into structured feature requests
  • Partner with the VP of Partner Growth to define the channel partner strategy and inform partner prioritization decisions
  • Identify expansion opportunities within existing partner footprints: new use cases, geographies, user segments, or product lines
  • Partner with Sales and Marketing to align channel activity to co-sell motions and joint go-to-market initiatives
  • Contribute to the buildout of scalable channel infrastructure: tier frameworks, health scoring, comp model inputs, and reporting tooling

Who You Are

You're the kind of person who...

  • Has operated in a channel, distribution, or platform partnerships role and understands what it takes to make indirect revenue models work
  • Thrives in the post-sale: you enjoy turning a signed partnership into a performing one and don't need the thrill of the new-logo chase to stay motivated. Proactive, not reactive.
  • Builds trust with external partners quickly. You're commercially fluent, technically credible, and curious about how their business works
  • Owns outcomes, not activities. You track GBV, conversion rates, and partner health, and you know what levers to pull when numbers move in the wrong direction
  • Is comfortable managing a diverse portfolio, able to prioritize across partners of different sizes, industries, and models without letting anything fall through the cracks; you have systems, not just good intentions
  • Is comfortable in ambiguity and can structure your own work without constant direction
  • Brings a point of view to the table in internal discussions. You advocate for your partners while holding Engine's commercial interests clearly in mind
  • Has a high bar for communication: written, verbal, and visual. You can synthesize a complex partner situation into a clear executive update

Experience & Qualifications

Required

  • 5+ years in partner growth, partner success, strategic account management, or channel partnerships, ideally in travel tech, fintech, SaaS, or a distribution-heavy business
  • Demonstrated track record managing complex, high-value B2B relationships with measurable GBV or revenue outcomes
  • Experience managing partners across more than one industry or partner type (e.g., associations, fintech/corporate card, marketplaces, distribution platforms) is a strong differentiator
  • Commercial acumen: comfortable with pricing negotiations, contract terms, and tier-based incentive structures
  • Strong data orientation: you use metrics to tell stories and drive decisions, and you're comfortable building your own analyses in Excel/Google Sheets

Preferred

  • Hands-on experience with partner commercial contracts, including structuring, negotiating, and renewing agreements with revenue-share terms, exclusivity, SLAs, and amendments, and partnering with Legal and Finance to get them across the line
  • Experience building partnerships playbooks, onboarding frameworks, or health scoring models, and familiarity with partner ecosystem tools like Crossbeam
  • Exposure to comp plan design or partner incentive structures (SPIFs, tier bonuses, go-live milestones)

Compensation & Structure

Role context

  • Compensation is structured as a base + variable model

The Director of Software Engineering owns the strategy, people, and delivery health of multiple engineering teams in the Security and Alarm portfolio. You will build and develop a bench of engineering managers, set engineering priorities with product, architecture, and business leaders, and hold your organization accountable for sustained delivery, team health, and technical quality at scale.

You will translate company goals into engineering priorities, represent engineering in senior cross-functional forums, and make sure your teams can deliver reliably and keep getting better. People and Organizational Leadership

Strategy and Communication

jobs.excerpt: About Baringa Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value.
jobs.description:
About Baringa

Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value. With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.

The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.

Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. The firm is known for its kind, curious experts who listen closely and care deeply about client success as they help clients transform energy markets, modernise financial platforms, expand telecoms and digital networks through advanced data analytics, enable digital services in government, and unlock growth in consumer sectors.

Certified as a Great Place to Work around the world, Baringa has been recognised by the Financial Times in 22 categories of its UK Leading Management Consultants rankings, and by Forbes for four consecutive years as one of the World’s Best Management Consulting Firms.

Our Technology team are looking for an experienced Infrastructure Operations Engineer to join the team.

Baringa’s TeCy Group (Technology & Cyber) is a global function supporting the firm as it enters new markets. We’re on a mission to develop great technology products and deliver great services. We’ve installed a new operating system for ourselves and rebooted what was a corporate IT department to an in-house technology company - transforming the way we work and opening the way to serve Baringa’s clients directly. We’re working on sustainability, committed to Net Zero in our supply-chain and services. We’re keeping our firm safe: protecting our data and our reputation. We are embarking upon and will be the driving force behind a new 3-Year digital strategy for the firm.

Yes, we’ve got a big job in the Baringa Technology & Cyber group.

So much to build on, so much to progress. So much to deliver. So much to play for!

Do you know what though? We’re going to do it. All of it and more. We have the support to drive change. We have a diverse group of 90 amazing technology & cyber professionals. We have the belief. We are going to do great things.

What you will be doing

We are seeking a skilled and proactive InfraOps Engineer to join our IT Operations team. This role is responsible for maintaining, optimizing, and securing our infrastructure across on-premises and cloud environments. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in systems administration, automation, cloud technologies and identity management, with some exposure to database operations.

You will help keep Baringa’s infrastructure reliable, secure and continually improving by solving complex incidents, supporting Windows and Azure services, and taking ownership of key services. You’ll use automation and collaborate across Technology & Cyber to strengthen operations and bring new services smoothly into support.

It’s a varied, hands-on role where you can troubleshoot, automate, strengthen resilience and contribute to meaningful improvements. You’ll have the freedom to take ownership, share your knowledge and make a visible impact within a supportive InfraOps team.

Infrastructure and Cloud Operations

  • Monitor, maintain, and troubleshoot servers, storage, and network systems.
  • Deploy, operate and improve Azure infrastructure services, including virtual machines, networking, storage, monitoring and Azure Virtual Desktop where applicable.
  • Implement cloud governance, cost optimization, and scaling strategies.
  • Explore and implement constant improvements of the infrastructure stack, in line with ITIL.

Database Operations

  • Administer and maintain MSSQL and Azure SQL databases.
  • Monitor performance and manage backups and restores.
  • Implement efficient user and group-based access control using SQL Server roles and Active Directory integration.
  • Ensure least-privilege access and regularly audit permissions.

User and Group Management

  • Manage user identities and group memberships across Active Directory and Azure AD.
  • Implement role-based access control (RBAC) for infrastructure and database resources.
  • Collaborate with Security and Compliance teams to enforce access policies.

Automation and Scripting

  • Automate infrastructure tasks using Azure, PowerShell, Bash, Python, or Terraform.
  • Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines for infrastructure provisioning.

Monitoring and Incident Response

  • Manage monitoring tools (e.g., SolarWinds).
  • Respond to incidents, perform root cause analysis, and implement fixes.

Security and Compliance

  • Apply patches and updates to infrastructure components.
  • Manage firewalls, access controls, and vulnerability scans.
  • Ensure compliance with internal policies and external regulations.
  • Compile and report infrastructure operations for audits such as ISO and CE+

Collaboration and Documentation

  • Work closely with DevOps, Security, and Application teams.
  • Document infrastructure configurations, procedures, and incident reports.
  • Take part in major incident management operations with the MIM.

Your skills and experience

  • Proven senior-level experience in infrastructure operations, systems administration and service ownership.
  • Strong hands-on experience supporting Microsoft Azure infrastructure, including virtual machines, networking, storage, monitoring, backup and recovery.
  • Strong Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID experience, including hybrid identity, role-based access, privileged access and access reviews.
  • Experience managing Windows Server services, including DNS, DHCP, certificates, file services, Group Policy and server lifecycle management.
  • Backup, restore and disaster recovery experience, including completing restores and participating in recovery exercises.
  • Operational networking knowledge, including IP addressing, routing, DNS, virtual networks, firewalls, VPNs and connectivity troubleshooting.
  • Experience with monitoring, patching and vulnerability management, including alert improvement, remediation prioritisation and risk evidence.
  • Strong incident, problem and change management skills, including ownership of complex incidents, root-cause analysis and controlled production changes.
  • Proficiency in scripting and infrastructure automation, particularly PowerShell, with suitable use of version control and peer review.
  • Excellent communication and documentation skills, with the ability to work across global teams, coach colleagues and produce clear technical and audit evidence.

What a career at Baringa will give you

Putting People First.

Baringa is a People First company and wellbeing is at the forefront of our culture. We recognise the importance of work-life balance and flexible working and provide our staff amazing benefits. Some of these benefits include:

  • Generous Annual Leave Policy: We recognise everyone needs a well-deserved break. We provide our employees with 5 weeks of annual leave, fully available at the start of each year. In addition to this, we have introduced our 5-Year Recharge benefit which allows all employees an additional 2 weeks of paid leave after 5 years continuous service.
  • Flexible Working: We know that the ‘ideal’ work-life balance will vary from person to person and change at different stages of our working lives. To accommodate this, we have implemented a hybrid working policy and introduced more flexibility around taking unpaid leave.
  • Corporate Responsibility Days: Our world is important to us, so all our employees get 3 every year to help social and environmental causes and increase our impact on the communities that mean the most to us.
  • Wellbeing Fund: We want to encourage all employees to take charge and prioritise their own wellbeing. We’ve introduced our annual People Fund to support this by offering every individual a fund to support and manage their wellbeing through an activity of their choice.
  • Profit Share Scheme: All employees participate in the Baringa Group Profit Share Scheme so everyone has a stake in the company’s success.

Diversity and Inclusion

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We believe that creating an environment where everyone feels a sense of belonging is central to our culture and that diversity is paramount to driving creativity, innovation, and value for our clients and for our people.

An award-winning workplace

You can be a part of our ‘Great Place to Work’ – with our commitment to women and well-being in the workplace for all. Click here to see some of our recent awards and how we’ve achieved this.

Using business as a force for good.

We maintain high standards of environmental performance and transparency, which can be seen through our commitment to Net Zero with our SBTI-verified Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions reduction targets and our support of the Better Business Act. We report our progress publicly and ensure that we are also externally assessed and scored through organisations like CDP and EcoVadis - helping us to continually identify where we can improve.

We have a long legacy of supporting the communities in which we work, and offer a variety of ways to contribute, by putting people first and creating impact that lasts. Our Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) agenda is about giving back to the communities in which we live and work by sharing our skills, talent and time. In essence, we aim to empower and encourage everyone in the firm to contribute to the things we care about, and support registered charities and organisations with a clear social or environmental purpose to increase the positive impact they can have.

Join us

All applications received will be reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team. We never rely solely on automated screening or AI tools to make hiring decisions. Your application will be considered for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, nationality, disability, age, faith or social background. We do not filter applications by university background and encourage those who have taken alternative educational and career paths to apply. We would like to actively encourage applications from those who identify with less represented and minority groups. We operate an inclusive recruitment process, ensuring reasonable adjustments where needed. Please contact a member of our Recruitment Team to discuss further.

jobs.description:
Remote (Global) | Full-Time Permanent | Machine Learning, Data Annotation & AI Workforce Operations

Every breakthrough AI model depends on people: the annotators, linguists, and domain experts who shape the data behind it. Someone has to find those people, at scale, across continents, without compromising on quality.

That someone could be you. Our client is looking for a talent leader to design the global hiring engine behind some of the most demanding AI data programs in the world. This isn't about filling seats. It's about building the workforce infrastructure that AI innovation runs on.

Why This Opportunity Matters

AI companies move fast, and their data needs move faster. One week a program needs multilingual LLM evaluators. The next week it needs LiDAR specialists, medical experts, or mathematicians, sometimes hundreds of them, ready to deliver at strict quality standards.

This role exists to make that possible. As Global Recruitment Lead, you'll own the system that turns client demand into a qualified, certified, ready-to-work talent pool across the US, Europe, LATAM, MENA, and APAC.

Your work feeds straight into delivery. When pipelines are healthy, programs launch on time, clients scale with confidence, and the business grows. This is a strategic leadership role, not a traditional HR position, and your impact will be visible from day one.

About Our Client

Our client combines human expertise with machine efficiency to deliver high-quality annotated data at scale. They help AI companies get faster, scalable results without sacrificing precision.

Their customers range from ambitious startups and academic institutions to Fortune 500 companies, in industries such as autonomous driving, retail, security, geospatial, and emerging LLM applications. They serve clients on every continent.

Even with that growth, they've held on to what sets them apart: transparency, fair pricing, personalized service, and a real commitment to exceptional results. The culture values innovation, collaboration, and excellence, and it gives people room to grow.

What You'll Own

  • The global hiring strategy. You'll design and run the talent approach for annotation, multilingual projects, LLM evaluation, LiDAR and Physical AI expertise, and specialized domains such as Legal, Medical, Maths, and Science.
  • Pipelines in five regions. You'll build and manage recruitment engines that deliver reliably across the US, Europe, LATAM, MENA, and APAC.
  • A flexible workforce ecosystem. You'll set up and scale vendor, freelancer, and distributed talent networks that can flex with changing project needs.
  • Speed without compromise. You'll lead high-volume, fast-turnaround hiring while holding the line on strict quality benchmarks.
  • How talent gets measured. You'll design structured screening frameworks, certification processes, and benchmarking systems that define what "qualified" means.
  • Capacity planning. You'll work with delivery and operations leaders to forecast workforce needs so talent is ready before demand arrives.
  • A smarter recruitment machine. You'll improve processes, automation tools, and ATS systems to make hiring faster and more efficient.
  • The numbers that matter. You'll track and report time-to-fill, time-to-certify, bench readiness, and pipeline health, and use that data to drive decisions.
  • Compliance across borders. You'll make sure distributed hiring meets contractual, regional, and data security requirements.
  • Ongoing improvement. You'll keep refining sourcing strategies to widen global talent coverage and scalability.

Requirements

  • You'll thrive in this role if you've already scaled distributed teams of 50 to 500+ people across international programs, and you know what it takes to do it again, only faster.
  • You'll do especially well if you bring 5 to 10 years of global talent acquisition experience, ideally in AI/ML, data services, SaaS, BPO, or tech-enabled platforms. You understand multilingual and contractor-based workforce models from the inside, not just in theory.
  • If you've hired for AI data annotation, LLM evaluation, CV/LiDAR, or domain-expert roles, you'll feel at home right away. Experience with global freelance marketplaces and distributed expert networks is a strong bonus.
  • You think in data. You build dashboards, read the signals, and adjust strategy based on evidence. You communicate clearly and manage stakeholders with confidence, whether that means pushing back on unrealistic timelines or getting operations, delivery, and vendors on the same page.
  • Most of all, you own outcomes. Fast-paced, high-growth environments energize you, and accountability feels like freedom, not pressure.
  • A Bachelor's degree in Business, Human Resources, Management, or a related field rounds out the profile.

Benefits

  • A foundational role. You won't be inheriting someone else's playbook. You'll build the international workforce engine from the ground up and put your mark on it.
  • Global reach. Your work will power AI programs that affect industries on every continent.
  • Visible strategic impact. In a high-growth setting, your results don't get lost. They show up in delivery, client success, and business growth.
  • A clear path forward. There's real room to grow into senior leadership roles as the organization scales.
  • Rewards tied to results. You'll get a competitive salary plus performance-based incentives linked to hiring success. Compensation is negotiable and benchmarked to your regional market, so pay stays fair and competitive.
  • Continued learning. Professional development support and learning opportunities are part of the package.
  • Flexibility that works. The role is fully remote, with working hours that combine your regional time zone with overlapping hours for global collaboration.

Ready to Build What AI Runs On?

If you're excited to design a global talent engine from scratch and see your strategy turn directly into business results, this is the kind of role that defines a career.

The start date is immediate, and our client is moving quickly. If you've scaled distributed teams before and you're ready to do it on a global stage, apply now and tell us about the pipelines you've built.

jobs.excerpt: Proposal No: UPGI-26-PR087Consultancy Type: Short Term Publication Date: 14/10/2026Clarifications Deadline: 26/10/2026Closing Date: 30/10/2026Consultants Location: Sub Saharan Africa 1.
jobs.description:
Proposal No: UPGI-26-PR087

Consultancy Type: Short Term

Publication Date: 14/10/2026

Clarifications Deadline: 26/10/2026

Closing Date: 30/10/2026

Consultants Location: Sub Saharan Africa

  1. Introduction

About BRAC International

BRAC is an award-winning international non-governmental development organisation with the vision of a world free from all forms of exploitation and discrimination, where everyone can realise their potential. BRAC is a leader in developing and implementing cost-effective, evidence-based programmes to assist poor and disadvantaged communities in low-income countries, including in conflict-prone and post-disaster settings. It is an organisation of and for the people of the Global South, pioneering new development and social enterprise approaches to equip communities to achieve prosperity. As well as being the world's biggest NGO by the number of staff and people directly reached, BRAC has regularly been ranked the number one NGO in the world by the Geneva-based NGO Advisor, an independent organisation committed to highlighting innovation, impact and governance in the non-profit sector.

About BRAC’s Work Scaling Graduation through Governments

The Graduation approach is a sequenced, adaptive set of interventions that together tackle multiple constraints that trap people in extreme poverty over a two-year period. By providing people with a productive asset to generate income, basic needs support, and ongoing, intensive coaching to unlock agency, know-how, and hope, the approach enables people to build lasting trajectories out of extreme poverty.

Pioneered by BRAC in 2002, Graduation now has more than 100 studies from 40+ countries, showing it achieves transformational impacts for participants across a wide variety of contexts. A long-term study of a programme in West Bengal found that ten years after starting the programme, participants saw roughly 4x gains in household consumption compared to programme investment outlays, which may go as high as 11x over their lifetimes if those gains persist, according to Nobel Laureates Abhijit Banerjee and Esther Duflo. In 2020, BRAC was named an Audacious Project by TED, receiving a catalytic investment to lift 21 million more people out of extreme poverty by 2030. BRAC is combating extreme poverty by partnering with governments across Asia and Africa to scale the proven Graduation approach. Watch the TED talk here.

With catalytic funding from Audacious, BRAC has successfully cultivated partnerships with governments in Africa and Asia over the last few years, resulting in new models of Graduation in India, Indonesia, the Philippines, Rwanda, and South Africa. Efforts are also underway in Ethiopia with exploration to support even wider government-led uptake. Demonstrating to governments Graduation’s potential to achieve greater, more lasting impact through existing poverty reduction programmes has helped unlock significantly more resources from government partners. Yet, massive cuts in development aid means less funding is available to support these programmes, making philanthropic capital all the more critical.

BRAC has found that flexible philanthropic funding can drive transformative, catalytic government investment. Philanthropic support presents a powerful leverage opportunity: Every $1 of philanthropic support can unlock $10 to $50 of public financing and generate $65 to $200 in long-term household income gains.

In a moment when progress on extreme poverty has stalled and public budgets are under pressure, Graduation offers something rare: life-changing results that justify greater investment, and investment that reaches millions more people than either sector could achieve alone.

  1. The Assignment

2.1 Purpose:

The purpose of this consultancy is to strengthen BRAC Ultra-Poor Graduation Initiative (UPGI)’s ability to understand, influence and support the public financing of government-led Graduation programs in Sub-Saharan Africa.

The consultant will help UPGI move beyond a general understanding of whether governments have sufficient fiscal space toward a more operational understanding of how public resources are prioritized, budgeted, financed, released and executed, and therefore how Graduation can realistically be financed and institutionalized within government systems.

The work of the consultant should help BRAC’s country teams answer the following questions:

  • What are the main fiscal, financing, and public financial management constraints governments face in scaling Graduation?

  • What public resources are already available, and where are there realistic opportunities to strengthen, redirect, or mobilize financing for Graduation?

  • How can this analysis help Country Leads better position their engagement with the government?

  • What opportunities exist to influence upstream external financing, particularly through the World Bank and African Development Bank?

  • What longer-term structure and capabilities should UPGI establish to support this work over the remainder of the SGGA program?

2.3 Scope of Work:

  • Conduct country macro-fiscal and public financing analysis across 7 countries in Africa, to deepen UPGI teams’ understanding of the fiscal and financing context for scaling government-led Graduation.

  • Pilot the country assessment in Rwanda first, producing an initial country analysis and working with the Rwanda Country Team and UPGI ELT to assess how to make the analysis most useful, what additional questions it should answer, and how the approach should be refined before applying it to the remaining six countries.

  • Based on lessons from the Rwanda pilot, adapt and apply the approach to six additional priority countries, producing concise, actionable country briefs for Country Leads and the whole of UPGI.

  • Assessment and recommendations on positioning in each country.

  • Advise country teams on relevant government budget and financing processes, including engagement with Ministries of Finance and other key actors.

  • Identify upstream opportunities for multilateral influencing: finding key modes of engagement to learn and shape directions of external funders (especially the World Bank and AfDB).

  • Design long-term UPGI capabilities to shape country level and external financing and advise UPGI on how to measure large-scale public investment to Graduation.

  • The assignment will include one trip each to Rwanda, Ethiopia, South Africa, and Tanzania to conduct research, make relevant connections with government and MDBs, and debrief country teams on key findings and implications for their work.

2.4 Deliverables

  1. Seven country briefs: Produce concise macro-fiscal, PFM, and public financing assessments for seven priority countries, beginning with Rwanda as a pilot. The briefs should identify key constraints, financing opportunities, and implications for the Country Leads’ engagement with government.

  2. Country Visits: Undertake one trip each to Rwanda, Ethiopia, South Africa, and Tanzania to better understand the country context, in order to inform research and key findings for the brief.

  3. Upstream multilateral financing recommendations: Practical recommendations for how UPGI should strengthen engagement with the World Bank, African Development Bank, and other relevant external funders to help shape financing and programming over the next decade.

  4. Long-term function design: Recommendations to UPGI on a set of options on how to structure long-term UPGI capabilities, and resourcing to sustain understanding and influence of macro-fiscal, PFM, and public financing function for the next decade. This will include some recommendations on how to measure the volumes of public finance being used towards Graduation.

2.5 Desired skills and competencies:

The candidate should meet the following criteria:

  • Deep knowledge of macro-fiscal dynamics and public finance in sub-Saharan Africa

  • Experience with AfDB, World Bank senior management and planning cycles, co-financing mechanisms and country engagement processes

  • Experience working alongside country-level programme teams — comfortable operating in a support and advisory role rather than leading engagement

  • Understanding of social protection and economic inclusion programming in the African context — does not need to be a Graduation specialist

  • Able to produce clear, actionable written assessments that Country Leads and Executive Leadership Team can act on.

  • Ideally 15 years or more of experience, ideally in macroeconomics and public financial management.

2.6 Level of Effort, Duration, and Location of the assignment:

Consultancy, to be finalized by 31 August 2027. Level of effort: 70 days total, 20 days in 2026 and 50 days in 2027.

Submission Requirements

Interested and eligible consultants may obtain further information via email between 0900 and 1600 hrs EAT, Monday to Friday, until 26 November 2026. Enquiries should be sent to , with a copy to , using the subject line “Macro Fiscal and Public Financial Management Consultant”

Submission Requirements:

  1. Mandatory documents

  2. Technical Proposal

  3. Financial Proposal

Interested applicants are encouraged to review the detailed RFP document for further information on the scope of work, requirements, and submission process.

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Engineer to take technical ownership of complex products and systems and raise the engineering bar across the team.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review code, solve difficult engineering problems, guide other engineers and drive major initiatives from idea to production.

You should be comfortable moving between architecture and implementation — making strong technical decisions while still being close enough to the code to execute when needed.

What You'll Own

  • Lead the technical design and execution of major products, features and engineering initiatives.

  • Design scalable, reliable and maintainable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Stay hands-on with engineering through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Make architecture decisions and technical trade-offs that balance speed, scalability, reliability and maintainability.

  • Break ambiguous product and technical problems into clear engineering solutions and execution plans.

  • Set a high bar for code quality, system design, testing, security, observability and production reliability.

  • Review technical designs and code from other engineers and provide clear, actionable feedback.

  • Mentor engineers and help strengthen technical capability across the team.

  • Identify technical risks, bottlenecks and architectural weaknesses before they become larger problems.

  • Work closely with engineering, product, design and AI teams to ship high-quality products quickly.

  • Improve engineering tooling, development practices and automation to increase team velocity.

  • Own systems beyond release — monitor production, investigate incidents, resolve root causes and continuously improve reliability.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with significant experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep technical expertise in one or more areas such as backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills with experience making technical decisions for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Proven experience leading major engineering projects or providing technical leadership to other engineers.

  • Comfortable reviewing code, debugging complex issues and working directly with production systems.

  • Able to explain complex technical decisions clearly and influence engineers across teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity and take ownership from problem definition through production.

  • Strong judgment around when to move quickly, when to simplify and when deeper engineering investment is required.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who want a leadership title but no longer want to write or review code.

  • People who only want to work within one narrow technical area.

  • Engineers who wait for complete specifications before starting.

  • Candidates who over-engineer solutions when a simpler approach would achieve the outcome.

  • Engineers who focus only on implementation without understanding the product or business problem.

  • People who avoid production incidents, difficult debugging or ownership after release.

  • Candidates who make vague claims about technical leadership without being able to explain what they personally designed, built, shipped or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for technical leaders with real engineering career highlights.

A strong highlight is not simply having a senior title or working at a famous technology company. A strong highlight means you personally designed, built, shipped or scaled a serious product, platform or system and can go deep into the technical decisions behind it.

You should be able to demonstrate both technical depth and technical leadership — someone who can solve difficult engineering problems personally while making the engineers around them stronger.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

You'll own test strategy end-to-end across a fast-moving codebase, build the automation frameworks that give engineering the confidence to ship daily, and be the voice for testability and reliability in every design conversation you're part of.

As a Senior Software Quality Engineer, your role will include:

  • Test framework ownership: Lead the design, development, and maintenance of automated test frameworks spanning backend services and UI, built to scale with a fast-growing product.

  • CI/CD integration: Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, etc.) so engineers get fast, high-confidence feedback on every change.

  • Exploratory testing: Run exploratory testing to catch usability issues, edge cases, and regressions that automation won't find on its own.

  • Parallel execution: Move across multiple projects at once in a startup environment where priorities shift, without losing rigor.

This role could be a fit for you if you bring:

  • Experience depth: 7+ years in QA or software testing, including 2+ years operating at a senior or staff level.

  • Ownership mindset: You spot what needs to happen and drive it forward without waiting to be told.

  • Startup fluency: Proven ability to stay calm under ambiguity and juggle competing priorities in a fast-moving environment.

  • Communication: Strong written and verbal skills, with the ability to advocate for quality across engineering and product.

  • CI/CD depth: Deep understanding of CI/CD systems and hands-on experience integrating automated test suites into pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or similar).

  • Kubernetes fluency: Working knowledge of Kubernetes environments and distributed systems, or a strong aptitude and willingness to learn quickly.

  • Debugging skill: Excellent analytical and debugging ability, particularly for backend and infrastructure-related issues.

Bonus points for:

  • Experience testing in tenant cluster or Tenant Isolation environments.

  • Prior experience owning QA at a startup through a period of rapid product growth.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

jobs.description:
Heifer International (“Heifer”) is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, status as a protected veteran, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with some form of disability.

About Heifer International

In 1944, Heifer International’s founder, Dan West, began outlining a simple but groundbreaking plan to tackle hunger around the world. West, a farmer from the Midwest and Church of the Brethren member, had recently returned from feeding weary refugees during volunteer service in the Spanish Civil War.

He had seen firsthand that giving people food was a short-term solution, whereas providing them with animals offered a steady supply of nutritious food for an entire family. His philosophy still inspires Heifer’s work today. Partnering with farmers across a range of different livestock and crops, we create unique solutions to local challenges.

Today, Heifer International has operations in 19 countries around the world, working alongside local farmers, business owners and their communities, as they mobilize and envision their futures. Together, we build inclusive, resilient economies, so communities can develop effective ways to end global hunger and poverty in a sustainable way.

To date, we have supported more than 42 million farming families across Africa, Asia and the Americas and in the past five years alone. We have worked alongside 2.7 million families to close the living income gap or set them on a path to doing so. Between now and 2030, we will support an additional 10 million people to reach a living income by scaling up our signature programs. To achieve this, Heifer International relies on its passionate, committed, and highly skilled staff.

ROLE FUNCTION

The Legal Drafting Senior Coordinator supports Heifer’s Legal Services department by drafting, reviewing, revising, and improving contracts, grant agreements, policies, procedures, training materials, and other transactional documents used in the jurisdictions where Heifer operates. Working under the direction and supervision of a licensed attorney, the Legal Drafting Senior Coordinator applies approved templates and standards, identifies issues for escalation, coordinates with internal stakeholders and local counsel, and supports negotiation, approval, and execution. The Legal Drafting Manager will collaborate with all of Heifer’s areas in this role, including the Americas, Africa, Europe, and Asia. Professional fluency in English and Spanish, including the ability to read, write, and discuss complex contractual and business matters in both languages, is required.

THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE

The Legal Drafting Senior Coordinator must lead and own assigned areas of responsibility and exercise sound judgment, accountability, adaptability, timeliness, attention to detail, and responsiveness.

RESPONSIBILITIES & DELIVERABLES

Drafting, Reviewing, and Improving Legal Documents (70%)

  • Drafting, reviewing, and improving various contracts, grant agreements, and transactional documents, under the direction and supervision of a licensed attorney, to be utilized in jurisdictions in which Heifer carries out its work. This may require coordinating with local counsel in countries where Heifer carries out its work. Deliverables include:
  • Independent Contractor Agreements
  • Grant and Project-related Agreements
  • Memoranda of Understanding
  • Confidentiality Agreements
  • Employment/Separation Agreements
  • License Agreements
  • Software/SaaS Agreements
  • Cooperation Agreements
  • Lease Agreements
  • Loan Agreements
  • Promissory Notes
  • Construction Agreements
  • Powers of Attorney
  • Waivers
  • Policies and Procedures
  • Training Materials
  • Best Practices
  • Various other agreements and legal documents

Training on Legal Contracts and Grants (20%)

  • Train Contract Specialists and other staff in matters related to contracts and grant agreements
  • Create, implement, and conduct other various grant and contract trainings

Miscellaneous Legal Tasks (10%)

  • Assist in maintaining legal templates
  • Assist in developing best practices
  • Review and verify invoices
  • May perform other job-related duties as assigned

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s Degree related to writing, business, and/or the legal field.
  • Minimum 6-7 years of substantive experience in drafting, reviewing, and improving contracts and grant agreements, including experience handling increasingly complex agreements with substantial independence.
  • Professional fluency in English and Spanish, including the ability to read, write, and discuss complex contractual and business matters in both languages.
  • Ability to draft, review, and improve contracts and grant agreements in a dynamic, demanding environment.
  • Preferred Requirements:
  • Experience in the legal field is preferred. Admission to practice law is not required for this non-attorney position.
  • Experience working or volunteering with nonprofit or mission-driven organizations.
  • General understanding of 501(c)(3) charities.
  • Previous nonprofit experience.

Most Critical Proficiencies:

  • Exceptional drafting, editing, proofreading, and plain-language communication skills.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Word and experience using organization-approved AI-assisted drafting and document-review tools.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Ability to manage administrative matters, including grant/contract workflow and database.

Essential Job Functions and Physical Demands:

  • Frequent in-person, telephonic, and electronic communication (both in the US and internationally).
  • Relate to, and communicate professionally and effectively with, a diverse group of individuals from various cultures.
  • Maintain a flexible schedule to accommodate time zone differences existing in an international organization.
  • Work under pressure, perform multiple tasks, and manage consistently competing priorities in a rapidly changing environment.

The expected range for candidates outside of the U.S. will align to Heifer’s pay scales for the individual country the candidate resides in. Please share your salary expectations in your application.

jobs.title: Customer Growth BDR
jobs.excerpt: The Opportunity: Every day, many of the world's largest companies buy the goods they run on through procurement systems like SAP Ariba, Coupa, and Jaggaer.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity:
Every day, many of the world's largest companies buy the goods they run on through procurement systems like SAP Ariba, Coupa, and Jaggaer. TradeCentric is the connectivity layer that makes that possible, linking B2B suppliers and their eCommerce platforms (Shopify, Salesforce Commerce, Adobe Commerce, OroCommerce, BigCommerce) directly to their buyers' eProcurement systems (SAP Ariba, Coupa, Jaggaer, Oracle, PeopleSoft, SAP). When suppliers connect through TradeCentric, they become easier to buy from, and they win more business.
Many of our customers are part of larger organizations: parent companies, sister companies, divisions, and regional operations that run their own P&L, their own commerce stack, and their own buying decisions. Most of those organizations are not yet TradeCentric customers. That is the opportunity.
As a Customer Growth Representative, you will be the bridge between the customers who already trust us and the parts of their organizations we have not yet reached. You will call into our existing customer base, map the corporate family behind each account, and uncover net-new opportunities at sister companies, new locations, and separate P&Ls. These are new-logo opportunities, distinct from the add-on business our Customer Success team manages, and you will hand them to Account Executives as a qualified pipeline.
Reporting to the BDR Manager, you will work as part of a win team with Account Executives, Solution Engineers, and Customer Success, using the Same Side Selling methodology to hand AEs well-qualified Sales Qualified Leads (SQLs) that turn into real deals.

Why You'll Love This Role:
  • Warm doors, not cold lists. You will open conversations with people who already know and value TradeCentric, and use that credibility to reach new buyers across their organization.
  • A real path to closing deals. A defined path to Account Executive, plus pathways into Account Management, Pre-Sales, Solution Consulting, or Sales Leadership.
  • Coaching that makes you better. Structured onboarding, ongoing coaching, and call reviews in Gong from leaders invested in your growth.
  • A role you help define. This is a new position at TradeCentric. Your playbook, insights, and results will shape how we grow inside our customer base.
  • Enterprise sales skills that last. You will learn to navigate complex corporate structures and multi-stakeholder deals across Mid-Market and Enterprise organizations.
Report to: BDR Manager
Pay Range: Base salary ranges from $65,000 to $75,000, with OTE of $100,000-$120,000. Final compensation is determined based on skills, experience, and qualifications.Work Location: This role is 100% remote.
While we prefer candidates based in the below city/states, we are open to considering candidates from other locations if you feel you meet the role’s qualifications. Don’t hesitate to apply if you’re excited about this opportunity and believe you’re a great fit!
-Raleigh, North Carolina
-Chicago, Illinois
-Boston, Massachusetts
-Charlottesville, Virginia
-Minneapolis, Minnesota

What You'll Do:

Map the Whitespace
  • Build corporate family maps for assigned customer accounts, identifying parent companies, subsidiaries, sister companies, acquisitions, divisions, and locations.
  • Identify which entities run a separate P&L, a separate eCommerce or ERP platform, or separate buyer relationships, and prioritize them by fit and potential.
  • Use intent data, trigger events, and AI research tools to spot new openings across the customer base, such as acquisitions, new facilities, new divisions, replatforming projects, and new buyer mandates.
  • Maintain account hierarchies and whitespace notes in Salesforce so every team member sees the same picture.
Work the Approved Customer Network
  • Call into existing customers but make new contacts for sister companies, new locations, or separate business units to learn how their broader organization sells and connects to buyers.
  • Work with the CSM team on introductions and referrals to decision makers at sister companies, new locations, and separate business units.
  • Run multichannel outreach (calls, email, LinkedIn, video) into newly identified entities, using customer proof points and internal success stories to open doors.
  • Execute and help build the sequences and messaging in a new Customer Growth playbook.
Qualify Like a Consultant
  • Lead discovery using Same Side Selling, uncovering desired results, issues, and business impact for each new entity.
  • Apply clear net-new criteria: a separate legal entity, a separate P&L or budget owner, a new location with its own buying or selling operation, or a separate commerce stack.
  • Route add-on business (additional trading partners, connections, or users under an existing account) to Customer Success rather than Sales.
  • Advance leads from SQL to SQO against the playbook's qualification criteria, and deliver clean, well-documented handoffs that set AEs up to win.
Protect the Relationship
  • Follow clear rules of engagement on ownership and timing.
  • Treat every customer call as a relationship moment, and route service issues, renewal risk, or satisfaction signals to the right owner quickly.
  • Capture customer insights (new initiatives, organizational changes, competitive activity) and share them with Sales leadership and Customer Success.
  • Join territory planning and account mapping sessions with AEs, Solution Engineers, and CSMs.
Own Your Pipeline
  • Track activity, account hierarchies, contact data, and disqualification reasons accurately in Salesforce and Gong.
  • Review SQL to SQO conversion rate, the share of your SQLs that AEs accept as SQOs, because quality matters as much as volume.
  • Share weekly updates on SQOs against target and whitespace coverage across your assigned accounts.
  • Work in a modern stack: Salesloft, Gong, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and AI research and prospecting tools.
  • With structured onboarding and coaching, you will reach full SQO productivity within 90 days of hire
How You'll Win
Success here is simple and visible. You are measured on:
  • Net-new SQOs generated from the existing customer base, by count, against monthly and quarterly targets.

What It Takes to Excel:

  • 1 to 3 years of BDR, SDR, or account development experience, B2B SaaS or technology preferred.
  • A track record of meeting or beating pipeline targets.
  • Strong research skills and the curiosity to untangle complex corporate structures.
  • Experience prospecting into multi-stakeholder, technically complex sales.
  • Confidence on the phone, with the judgment to balance new business goals and customer trust.
  • A collaborative style that builds strong working relationships with Customer Success and Account Management.
  • Strong CRM discipline, Salesforce experience preferred.
  • AI fluency, using generative AI and signal data tools to research smarter and prospect faster.
  • The organization to prioritize competing activities without dropping the ball.
  • A goal-oriented, positive, self-starting mindset with a record of ownership.
Bonus points for
  • Experience in account-based or install-base selling.
  • Exposure to eCommerce, eProcurement, iPaaS, or data integration technology.
  • Familiarity with corporate hierarchy tools such as ZoomInfo, D&B Hoovers, or Salesforce account hierarchies.
  • Training in Same Side Selling or a similar consultative methodology.

Company Benefits

At TradeCentric, we have a strong and innovative team dedicated to transforming the way our clients do business. It is our people who make it happen and we strive to take care of our employees in every way we can. Below is a list of benefits that are offered to employees, once eligibility is met:
