Job Title - Lead Specialist, Corporate Communications

Description
Shape Pearson’s story across virtual learning and enterprise priorities in a strategic, hands-on role spanning integrated, executive and issues communications. Also known in the market as Corporate Communications Manager, Integrated Communications Manager, Strategic Communications Manager or Senior Communications Manager.

About the role

Pearson is looking for a strategic and hands-on communications professional to help shape, protect and enhance our reputation. This newly created role will support our Virtual Learning business while contributing to wider priorities including Career Readiness, Workforce Readiness and AI Innovation.

You will work across external, internal and executive communications, connecting business activity to Pearson’s wider corporate story. Success in this role requires strong strategic thinking combined with the ability to personally deliver high-quality communications materials, executive briefings and stakeholder content.

This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys creating structure, bringing stakeholders together and turning complex business activity into clear, engaging and impactful communications.

What you'll do

  • Lead proactive and reactive communications across PR, internal communications, social media, customer communications, public affairs and crisis communications.
  • Develop narratives, messaging frameworks and content aligned to Pearson’s corporate priorities and business objectives.
  • Support Pearson’s Virtual Learning business while connecting activity to wider themes including Career Readiness, Workforce Readiness and AI Innovation.
  • Partner proactively with stakeholders across Marketing, Product, Sales, Media Relations, Government Relations, HR and Corporate Communications.
  • Identify upcoming launches, conferences, campaigns, opportunities and potential reputational risks, ensuring the right teams are aligned and informed.
  • Prepare senior leaders for media opportunities, events, presentations and all-hands meetings through briefing memos, talk tracks, presentations and supporting communications materials.
  • Provide communications support for executive leadership communications, including presentations, internal messaging and executive social content.
  • Manage issues and crisis communications planning and response activities.
  • Monitor media, stakeholder sentiment and reputational risks, using insight to inform communications strategies and recommendations.
  • Produce polished, executive-ready materials in Microsoft Word and PowerPoint with a consistently high attention to detail.

What we're looking for

  • Broad experience across Corporate, Strategic or Integrated Communications rather than a single-channel communications specialism.
  • Proven ability to balance strategic communications planning with hands-on execution.
  • Strong narrative development skills and experience adapting key messages for multiple audiences while maintaining message consistency.
  • Experience working across multiple stakeholder groups, including customers, employees, policymakers, investors and senior leaders.
  • Strong B2B communications experience. Additional B2B2C or consumer-facing communications experience would be advantageous.
  • Experience supporting executive communications, leadership events, media preparation and thought leadership activity.
  • Experience managing issues, reputation or crisis communications in a complex organisation.
  • A proactive mindset with the ability to identify opportunities, connect stakeholders and drive activity forward without waiting for a detailed brief.
  • Excellent writing, editing and storytelling skills, with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Strong Microsoft Word and PowerPoint capabilities.
  • Practical awareness of AI in communications, SEO, AEO, GEO and the strategic use of social media.

Particularly attractive backgrounds

  • Education, Higher Education, EdTech or other regulated industries.
  • Corporate Communications experience within consulting or professional services organisations such as Accenture, McKinsey, BCG or similar firms.
  • Public Affairs, Government Relations or reputation management experience.

Location & Working Pattern

United States | Remote

The successful candidate will support Pearson’s North America business while collaborating across a global organisation. Flexible working arrangements will apply in line with Pearson policy and business requirements.

Salary

Compensation at Pearson is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and specific location. As required by the California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York State, New York City, Vermont, Washington State, and Washington DC laws, the pay range for this position is as follows:The minimum full-time salary range is between $75,000 - $115,000.This position is eligible to participate in an annual incentive program, and information on benefits offered is here.Applications will be accepted through September 13th 2026. This window may be extended depending on business needs.

Why join Pearson?

This is a rare opportunity to help shape communications across one of the world's leading learning companies. You'll work at the intersection of education, workforce readiness and AI innovation, partnering with senior leaders to tell compelling stories that influence customers, employees, policymakers and stakeholders globally.

If you enjoy turning complex business priorities into clear communications, building relationships across teams and delivering work that genuinely makes an impact, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.excerpt: About Xanadu:Xanadu’s mission is to build quantum computers that are useful and available to people everywhere.
jobs.description:
About Xanadu:Xanadu’s mission is to build quantum computers that are useful and available to people everywhere.

At Xanadu, we are learners, innovators, researchers, collaborators, and problem solvers. We are creating something that has never been built before. What we are doing is extremely hard, the classic moon shot. Few people in their life will be able to be a part of something like this, where if we are successful, the technologies we develop will solve some of the world’s most challenging problems, and literally change the world. That is something to be excited about!

Your role and responsibilities:As a quantum scientist, you will join a technical team of scientists dedicated to unlocking the real-world impact of fault-tolerant quantum computers. You will contribute to discovering cutting-edge quantum algorithms, rigorously optimizing their performance, and identifying valuable applications across a variety of industries. Whether your primary strength is pioneering algorithms or uncovering novel applications, this role thrives at the intersection of both. At Xanadu, this research is conducted alongside industry, government, and academic partners, requiring close collaboration with software, hardware, and business development teams across the company.

In more detail, you will focus deeply on:
  • Designing and pioneering innovative quantum algorithms tailored for fault-tolerant quantum computers for applications related to computational chemistry.
  • Radically improving algorithm efficiency by reducing qubit counts, gate complexity, and overall resource requirements
  • Identifying high-value applications targeted at our chemistry-related focus industries.
  • Demonstrating the feasibility and scalability of new algorithms and applications through rigorous resource estimation and comparison to state-of-the-art classical methods.
  • Collaborating with PennyLane software developers to create state-of-the-art tools for quantum algorithms research.
Regardless of your specific focus areas, you will consistently:
  • Author high-quality scientific papers, technical reports, and comprehensive documentation.
  • Generate valuable intellectual property and actively support the filing of related patents.
  • Present your research findings to strategic partners and at premier conferences and events.

Basic qualifications and experience:
  • PhD in Chemistry, Physics, or a related quantitative discipline — or equivalent practical experience.
  • Strong track record of research accomplishments in computational chemistry and quantum computing, evidenced by publications, patents, or technical work.
  • Deep knowledge of quantum chemistry methods for ground and excited states, such as DFT, CASSCF/CASCI, MRCI, DMRG, Coupled Cluster, QMC, etc.
  • Knowledge of fundamental concepts in quantum algorithms, such as Hamiltonian simulation, Trotter product formulas, quantum signal processing, linear combination of unitaries, amplitude amplification, quantum phase estimation, and quantum read-only memories.
  • Expertise in application areas related to quantum chemistry, materials science, pharmaceuticals, etc.
  • Capacity to thrive in an interdisciplinary team environment and drive independent research when required.
  • Excellent communication skills, with a proven ability to convey complex technical ideas to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
  • Strong self-management skills to balance individual project priorities, deadlines, and deliverables in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred qualifications and experience:
  • Experience performing constant-factor resource estimation for fault-tolerant quantum algorithms.
  • Experience in using and/or developing quantum chemistry software including but not limited to PySCF, Gaussian, Q-Chem, ORCA, Psi4, NWChem, MOLCAS, GAMESS, etc.
  • Experience collaborating with industry or government partners.
  • Strong software development and scientific programming skills in Python and HPC expertise.

jobs.description:
About Us

Zoo is building the next generation of hardware design tools redefining how hardware products are designed, developed, and built. Our platform combines a modern, cloud-native CAD environment with AI-powered engineering workflows, helping teams design, iterate, and manufacture products faster than ever before. We are headquartered in Los Angeles, CA with both a local and remote team. We were founded and incubated by Embedded Ventures in 2021.

About You

We’re looking for curious, innovative, and ambitious self-starters to join our growing team to help us bring our mission to life. We think you’ll thrive on our team if you’re:

  • Curious at your core, with an eagerness to learn and do things differently
  • Customer-focused, always thinking about ways to improve the user experience
  • Able to operate autonomously and work asynchronously, while also being an effective team player

About The Role

As a Senior Frontend Engineer at Zoo, you'll play a crucial role in the development and enhancement of our novel open-source CAD modeling app, Zoo Design Studio. This unique, DSL-driven application leverages traditional CAD UI for code generation/editing while streaming a 3D scene from our remote graphics engine. This is a "back of the front-end" role, where your efforts will be instrumental in creating and gluing features together from our UI that drives DSL code-mods, triggering executions with our Rust/Wasm DSL, or interfacing with our backend's WebSocket API and doing so in an extensible way. We're looking for a seasoned Engineer with substantial experience building highly performant, scalable web applications with a deep understanding of performance optimization techniques. This is an awesome opportunity to significantly impact one of our core products during this critical phase of growth for our team.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop and optimize the frontend of our modeling app, focusing on performance and user experience
  • Collaborate with backend teams to design and implement robust APIs that support the app's code-driven design functionality
  • Enhance the app's UI/UX by leveraging Typescript, React, and XState, ensuring that the interface is both powerful and easy to use
  • Develop delightful CodeMirror extensions that bridge the gap between the user's code and the 3d-model
  • Implement advanced AST/code-mods, CodeMirror enhancements, and deep integration with WebAssembly (Wasm) for performance improvements
  • Utilize Xstate for state management to maintain app consistency and reliability across various user interactions
  • Apply a deep understanding of JavaScript and browser internals to improve app functionality and performance

What You’ll Need

  • B.S. in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent professional experience
  • Substantial experience in frontend software development building complex, highly performant and scalable applications
  • Strong proficiency in Typescript and React, with a portfolio or examples of complex applications built using these technologies
  • Deep knowledge of JavaScript and its internal workings and performance optimization techniques
  • Familiarity with WebAssembly (Wasm) and its use in web applications for performance enhancements
  • Understanding of browser internals across major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Chromium, Brave, etc.) and their impact on application performance and compatibility
  • Knowledge of Xstate or similar state management libraries

Nice to Have

  • Proficiency with Rust
  • Experience with CodeMirror6
  • Experience with ASTs even if custom ESLint rules
  • Experience with WebGL or web graphics
  • A background in geometry and/or experience with design-based software

The salary range for this role is provided below. The final offer will depend on multiple factors including candidate experience, skills, expertise, and market data. Compensation may vary by geography.

In addition to salary, we offer competitive equity as well as a full benefits package which may vary by geography as well.

Salary Range
$145,000—$195,000 USD

Zoo is an equal-opportunity employer committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. The Zoo team is made up of incredibly talented and unique individuals from across the globe. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, Veteran status, age, or any other trait that unfairly targets a group of people. We encourage everyone interested in our mission to apply!

jobs.description:
Director, Content Accessibility

College Board – Learning & Assessment

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type: This is a full-time position

About the Team

The Content Accessibility team at College Board has the privilege and responsibility of ensuring that College Board assessments are accessible for individuals with disabilities. Our work is both specialized and broad: we work with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to write and review image descriptions, consult with technology teams to improve accessibility supports in authoring tools, and collaborate with accessibility and accommodations specialists across the organization to ensure test content meets policy and the needs of test-takers. We not only advocate for universal design, we live it.

About the Opportunity

As a Director, Content Accessibility, you coach a team of writers and reviewers who bridge the gap between students who use assistive technology to take College Board assessments and the makers of College Board assessments. By bridging that gap, your team ensures every test question meets accessibility guidelines.

Your attitude is can-do: you write and review image descriptions and evaluate caption tracks, you construct reader scripts and braille maps, you apply headings when the content requires them. Moreover, you take on the team’s most complex and high-stakes work yourself. You do the work because leading by example helps the team excel. Ultimately, in Content Accessibility, everything you do is focused on one goal: ensuring College Board assessments are accessible so that all students, no matter their ability, can show what they know and can do. You can say with confidence that the work of your team is a primary reason College Board is an industry leader in accessible testing.

In this role, you will:

Lead and develop a team (30%)

  • Lead a team of four specialists responsible for the accessibility of assessment content across all College Board assessments.
  • Own day-to-day direction for the team. Assign and balance workloads, set priorities across competing program deadlines, and adjust plans as schedules shift, in partnership with the Senior Director and program leads.
  • Track and manage progress to goals, and provide coaching and support to ensure team members meet and exceed goals, remain engaged, and contribute meaningfully to our mission.
  • Cultivate an inclusive and high achieving culture that enables all team members to live out College Board’s Operating Principles.
  • Embody College Board’s Manager Expectations in your work.
  • Participate in hiring, onboarding, and training, and help shape team roles and structure as needs evolve.
  • Conduct regular check-ins and reviews and coach team members through feedback, professional development plans, and stretch assignments.

Be an expert practitioner (40%)

  • Write accessible test content (including image descriptions, reader scripts, and braille transcription notes), maintaining the highest standards of quality and care, for College Board assessments. Personally adopt the hardest cases for yourself.
  • Review and remediate test content to conform to Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), ensuring all tests meet Section 504 and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements. Adapt strategically when content and standards don’t easily align.
  • Act as the team's authority on accessible-content standards, making final calls on edge cases when guidance is unclear or absent.
  • Review and remediate test-adjacent content (e.g., research studies, scoring guidelines) to conform to WCAG, ensuring all publications meet Section 504 and ADA requirements.
  • Set priorities for and maintain image description guidelines, authoring standards and practices (e.g., for mode transformations), documentation, presentations, and tools (e.g., user personas).
  • Lead quality-control, accessibility, and usability reviews of tests and applications, identifying patterns and root causes rather than one-off errors.
  • Maintain advanced proficiency in authoring tools and assistive technology, and advise the team on best practices.

Shape strategy, standards, and cross-functional practice (30%)

  • Contribute to Content Accessibility strategy and long-term planning as part of the team's leadership group, and lead execution of initiatives within your team's scope.
  • Synthesize accessibility research, web standards, and user-experience findings into clear evidence-based recommendations to improve tooling, processes, and authoring standards. Present and advocate for those recommendations to program and organization leadership.
  • Represent Content Accessibility, including the team’s aims, standards, constraints, and risk considerations, in planning conversations with program, product, and technology teams. Ensure accessibility is built into all processes, tools, and assessments.
  • Educate and mentor others about universal design, accessibility, and accommodations, such as through presentations and trainings.
  • Drive pilots of new tools, workflows, and technologies (including AI) that improve the quality, efficiency, or accessibility of test content.
  • Lead cross-team projects or serve on them as the accessibility subject matter expert.

About You

To qualify for this role, you must have:

  • 6+ years of experience in accessibility or accommodations-focused roles, technical writing, or assessment content writing, with at least 4 years specifically in accessibility or accommodations-related work (e.g., accessibility specialist, inclusive designer, Section 508 compliance analyst)
  • Experience leading people or work, such as supervising, mentoring, training, or leading projects.
  • Excellent written communication skills, with demonstrated experience writing or editing (e.g., technical writer or editor).
  • A strategic and inclusive leadership style: you set clear priorities, build effective team structures, plan for future needs, and foster a culture of belonging.
  • A proven ability to drive performance and growth: you set high expectations, deliver real-time, evidence-based feedback, and coach team members to take smart risks, stretch their skills, and achieve meaningful impact.
  • Excellent verbal communication skills, including facilitating meetings and presenting remotely and in-person to leaders and cross-functional audiences.
  • Demonstrated success handling complex, ambiguous, or high-stakes work with sound judgment and autonomy.
  • Adept problem-solving skills, including using data to inform decisions and actions.
  • Proven ability to build relationships and influence others to action.
  • Experience creating or maintaining accessibility standards or guidelines.
  • Fluency in web-content accessibility (WCAG, ARIA) and/or universal design.
  • Strong organization and prioritization skills and the proven ability to move forward multiple projects in concert, both independently and as a member of the team
  • Outstanding curiosity about emerging trends and best practices in web standards and accessibility
  • Certified Professional in Accessibility Core Competencies (CPACC) certification or Web Accessibility Specialist (WAS) certification preferred
  • Bachelor’s degree required
  • The ability to travel 1–3 times a year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $80,000 –$135,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

jobs.excerpt: About TJM LabsTJM Labs is building the digital workforce for pharmacy.
jobs.description:
About TJM Labs

TJM Labs is building the digital workforce for pharmacy.

Pharmacies are being asked to do more with fewer resources. Prescription volumes are growing, margins are tightening, and talented pharmacy teams spend too much of their day on repetitive operational work.

We're changing that.

TJM Labs builds AI-powered automation designed specifically for pharmacy. Our technology works within the systems pharmacies already use to automate repetitive workflows and create more capacity for pharmacists and pharmacy technicians to focus on the work that actually requires them.

As our customer base grows, we need people who can help pharmacies get answers quickly, understand when something isn't working as expected, and connect what the customer is experiencing with the technical teams who can solve it.

About the Role

We're looking for a Pharmacy Bot Support Specialist to provide responsive, thoughtful day-to-day support to pharmacies using TJM automation.

You'll work as part of a customer pod alongside Customer Success Managers, Implementation Leads, and technical teams.

This is not an account ownership role. You won't own the customer relationship, customer strategy, or implementation project.

Instead, you'll be one of the first people our pharmacy customers turn to when they have a question, need help, or tell us, 'The bot isn't doing what we expected.' Your job is to figure out what that actually means.

Sometimes the answer will be straightforward. Other times, you'll need to ask questions, understand the pharmacy workflow, gather examples, look at system information, reproduce the behavior, and document what you've learned so our technical teams can investigate efficiently.

You don't need to be an engineer. You do need to be technically curious, comfortable troubleshooting, an excellent communicator, and willing to keep asking questions until you understand what's actually happening.

What You'll Do

1. Be a Responsive First Point of Support

You'll help manage incoming day-to-day communication from pharmacy customers across our support channels.

  • Respond promptly and professionally to customer questions and reported issues.
  • Ask thoughtful follow-up questions to understand exactly what the customer is experiencing.
  • Gather the information needed to determine whether something is a question, training issue, workflow issue, configuration issue, product issue, or potential defect.
  • Help customers resolve issues that can be addressed without engineering involvement.
  • Set clear expectations about what happens next when additional investigation is required.
  • Keep customers updated rather than leaving them wondering whether anyone is working on their issue.
  • Close the loop once an issue has been resolved.

You won't be expected to have every answer. You will be expected to take responsibility for getting the information to the right person and making sure the question doesn't disappear.

2. Investigate Before You Escalate

One of the most important parts of this role is turning a customer-reported problem into something our technical teams can efficiently investigate.

  • Ask targeted questions about what happened before, during, and after the reported issue.
  • Gather specific examples, timestamps, prescription or workflow context, screenshots, and other appropriate information.
  • Understand what the customer expected to happen versus what actually happened.
  • Review available system activity, configurations, logs, and other troubleshooting information.
  • Attempt to reproduce reported behavior when appropriate.
  • Determine whether the issue affects one scenario or a broader workflow.
  • Check known issues and available documentation before escalating.
  • Document what you've already investigated so another team doesn't have to start from zero.

Your goal is to make sure engineering spends its time solving technical problems rather than trying to figure out what the problem is.

3. Create Excellent Technical Support Tickets

When an issue needs to move to engineering or another technical team, you'll make sure they receive a clear, actionable ticket.

  • What is happening — and what should be happening instead?
  • Which pharmacy and workflow are affected?
  • When did it happen, and is it reproducible?
  • What specific examples demonstrate the problem?
  • What troubleshooting has already been completed?
  • Is there a workaround, and how is this affecting the pharmacy's operation?

A great escalation means the technical team can begin investigating without immediately coming back for basic information.

4. Understand the Pharmacy Behind the Problem

Software support at TJM requires more than understanding software. You need to understand pharmacy.

  • Use your knowledge of pharmacy operations and pharmacy management systems to put customer questions into context.
  • Learn how each customer's TJM automation fits into its pharmacy operation and use that understanding to troubleshoot more effectively.

5. Communicate Clearly Through Resolution

Great support isn't only about solving the problem. It's also about what the customer experiences while we're solving it.

  • Explain technical information in clear, plain language.
  • Provide updates while issues are being investigated.
  • Avoid making promises before you have the information to make them.
  • Let customers know what we need from them and why.
  • Communicate internally when an issue may have broader customer impact.
  • Bring in the Implementation Lead or CSM when an issue crosses into their area of ownership.
  • Help diffuse frustration through responsiveness, empathy, and clear communication.
  • Confirm that the customer is actually seeing the expected behavior before considering an issue resolved.

6. Know When to Pull in the Pod

You'll work closely with Customer Success Managers and Implementation Leads, but each role has a different job.

  • Customer Success Managers own the strategic customer relationship, overall customer health, and escalations.
  • Implementation Leads own the day-to-day execution of implementations, including workflow documentation, implementation requirements, stakeholder coordination, QA, and go-live.
  • Pharmacy Bot Support Specialists provide day-to-day product support, investigate reported problems, gather the information needed to troubleshoot them, resolve what they can, and create high-quality escalations when technical assistance is required.

7. Help Us Spot Patterns

Individual support conversations can tell us a lot about our product.

  • Issues that appear repeatedly across customers.
  • Areas where customers consistently need additional training.
  • Workflows that generate frequent questions.
  • Product behavior that creates confusion.
  • Documentation or support resources we should improve.
  • Potential product enhancements.
  • Opportunities to prevent future support issues.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

  • 2+ years of experience working in a pharmacy environment, such as retail, specialty, mail-order, hospital, long-term care, or compounding.
  • Hands-on familiarity with pharmacy workflows and pharmacy management systems.
  • Technical curiosity and a genuine interest in figuring out how things work.
  • A methodical approach to problems and excellent follow-up questions.
  • Clear writing and the ability to document details someone else needs to act.
  • Patience and professionalism when someone is frustrated.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple customer questions and support issues.
  • Comfort working independently in a remote environment, screen sharing, video meetings, and learning new software.
  • Understanding of the importance of appropriately handling PHI and other sensitive healthcare information.

Pharmacy Technician Experience Is Highly Desired

Current or previous pharmacy technician experience is highly desired. Registered or certified pharmacy technicians are strongly encouraged to apply.

If you've worked in a pharmacy, you understand that 'the prescription didn't process correctly' could mean a dozen different things, and you know the questions to ask before deciding something is actually wrong with the pharmacy management system.

Pharmacy Management System Experience

Hands-on familiarity with pharmacy management systems is required for this role.

Experience with systems such as PioneerRx, PrimeRx, Rx30, Computer-Rx, FrameworkLTC, QS/1, or similar pharmacy management platforms is particularly valuable.

Nice to Have

  • Previous software or technical support experience.
  • Experience training pharmacy staff on technology or workflows.
  • Experience supporting software implementations.
  • Familiarity with Jira, Zendesk, ServiceNow, or similar tools.
  • Experience reviewing logs, configurations, or system activity.
  • Basic familiarity with Windows, networking, integrations, or software troubleshooting.
  • Experience with healthcare technology, workflow automation, or AI-powered technology.
  • Experience in specialty, compounding, long-term care, mail-order, or high-volume retail pharmacy.

What You Don't Need

You don't need to know how to code.

You don't need to be an engineer.

You don't need to be a project manager.

You don't need to own a book of business.

You don't need previous experience working with AI.

You don't need to arrive knowing TJM's technology.

You do need to understand pharmacy, enjoy technology, communicate exceptionally well, and be curious enough to keep digging when the first answer doesn't make sense. We'll teach you the rest.

You'll Probably Love This Role If...

Someone saying 'it's broken' immediately makes you want to know exactly what they were doing when it broke.

You're the person in the pharmacy people call over when something weird happens with the computer.

You ask, 'Can you show me?' a lot.

You enjoy figuring out why something happened almost as much as fixing it.

You know that 'it happens all the time' is not quite enough information to troubleshoot a problem.

You can talk comfortably with a pharmacy technician one minute and clearly document the same issue for an engineer the next.

You don't throw an issue over the fence to engineering and consider your job done.

There's something deeply satisfying to you about finally figuring out why the weird thing was happening.

Why TJM Labs

You'll join a fast-growing company working on a very real problem in healthcare. You'll see our automation working inside real pharmacies and taking repetitive work off the shoulders of pharmacists and pharmacy technicians.

For the right person, this can be a path from using pharmacy technology every day to becoming someone who helps shape how that technology works for pharmacies.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Remote-first work environment
  • The opportunity to work at the intersection of pharmacy, healthcare, and AI
  • Meaningful opportunity to learn and grow as TJM Labs continues to scale

jobs.excerpt: About CheckmateCheckmate is a restaurant technology solution provider that has continually evolved over time.
jobs.description:
About Checkmate

Checkmate is a restaurant technology solution provider that has continually evolved over time. We started in 2017 by integrating 3rd party platforms to the POS systems of restaurants. At that time, there were multiple 3rd party platforms like GrubHub, UberEats, DoorDash, Postmates, Caviar, and even Amazon!

This was the photograph that started it all!

We have since then continually evolved to add multiple products to our portfolio, the primary ones being first party ordering solutions like web and app ordering, kiosks and catering. We have now recently moved into three new exciting products: Digital Menu Boards, Phone Ordering AI and Drive thru AI. We form a very core part of the restaurant technology ecosystem, and are continually adding more and more digital solutions for the restaurant brands to increase their sales.

Our revolutionary enterprise menu management system, Everyware, truly unlocks the potential of menus and how it can be customized for each individual digital channel. As you can see, this is a company that continually evolves and adapts and today we are powering digital ordering solutions for some of the largest brands in the world.

We have been called the "north star of vendors" as we truly believe that technology is just a method by which we service the customers, it does not form the entirety of it. Service is a big component of what we provide to our customers, which is inherently believed by every single team member here. We are doing a lot of exciting things, including application of AI in our products and systems, using experimentation at scale to determine what works for our clients and ML to analyze and productize the massive amount of data we have. Each individual here makes a difference and has a valuable contribution. Key traits here are ownership and drive. Join us if you think you have them.

About the Role

As a Vice President of Engineering, you will operate as a player/coach and join a collaborative team of VPs of Engineering reporting directly to the Chief Technology Officer (CTO). In this role, you will lead globally distributed software engineering teams driving the execution, architectural integrity, and delivery of core product initiatives built on cloud-native architectures in AWS.

Drawing on your experience in high-growth SaaS and web-based startup environments, you will serve as a key technical leader across the organization, partnering closely with Product leadership, Data Analytics, and cross-functional teams to build high-performance, scalable software that drives business growth. You will also be at the forefront of modern engineering management, actively driving teams to adopt AI-driven development practices to increase velocity, code quality, and developer productivity.

Essential Job Functions

Global Engineering Leadership & Talent

  • Lead, mentor, and grow distributed software engineering teams located across global regions, with direct leadership experience overseeing development teams based in India.
  • Foster a high-performance, inclusive culture that excels across time zones, ensuring clear communication, alignment, and operational execution.
  • Champion and integrate modern AI-driven development tools and workflows (e.g., AI coding assistants, automated test generation, AI-assisted code reviews) to accelerate execution and upskill engineering talent.
  • Recruit, develop, and retain top talent, establishing clear career progression pathways and coaching engineering managers and technical leads.

Technical Strategy & Architectural Excellence

  • Drive architectural vision and technical design for your product domain, ensuring scalable, secure, and cost-efficient deployments natively on AWS.
  • Champion modern engineering best practices, including design standards, code reusability, automated testing, system performance, and technical debt remediation.
  • Partner with platform and infrastructure leaders to ensure software designs integrate smoothly into company-wide CI/CD pipelines and cloud infrastructure.

Process Development, Continuous Improvement & Team Metrics

  • Design, document, and own the engineering operating model for a team of engineers, including sprint and release cadence, planning and estimation, code review standards, branching and deployment practices, and definition-of-done criteria.
  • Establish lightweight, scalable processes that fit a remote, globally distributed team
  • Define, instrument, and report on team performance metrics. These cover delivery (deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, time to restore service), quality (escaped defects, test coverage, incident volume), predictability (commitment accuracy, cycle time), and team health (engagement, on-call load, attrition).
  • Run a regular continuous improvement cycle, including retrospectives, post-incident reviews, and quarterly process assessments. Turn findings into prioritized, owned improvement initiatives with measurable outcomes.
  • Measure the impact of AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code, AI code review, automated test generation) on velocity, quality, and developer experience. Use the results to refine adoption practices and guidance.
  • Maintain a sustainable balance between feature delivery, technical debt remediation, and operational work through explicit capacity allocation and regular roadmap trade-off discussions with Product.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Process

  • Work closely with Product Management, Data Analytics, and Customer Success teams to align technical roadmaps with business objectives, user experience goals, and feature releases.
  • Collaborate with peer VPs of Engineering under the CTO to establish consistent engineering standards, shared technical frameworks, and cross-team processes.
  • Manage strategic software vendor and third-party partner relationships (e.g., outsourced talent, specialized tools) to scale capability in a fast-moving SaaS environment.
  • Implement and continuously refine Agile processes to reduce friction, increase delivery velocity, and elevate product quality.

Requirements

  • 12+ years of progressive software engineering experience, with 5+ years in senior engineering leadership roles managing engineering managers and cross-functional teams.
  • 7+ years hands-on experience with Ruby on Rails ecosystem patterns, performance tuning, or legacy/modern Rails application scaling is a strong plus.
  • 7+ years hands-on experience with asynchronous processing and architectures
  • 5+ years working in and managing a 100% remote based team
  • Proven SaaS / web-based startup experience, with a track record of thriving in fast-paced, high-growth environments where speed and adaptability are critical.
  • Demonstrated experience leading engineering team members globally having deep familiarity with cross-cultural team management.
  • Strong track record of collaborating with peer engineering leaders and senior stakeholders under executive direction.
  • Strong, proven expertise in building and scaling applications hosted on AWS (Amazon Web Services).
  • Experience actively implementing and driving engineering teams to adopt AI-driven development practices (e.g., Claude Code) to improve workflow and output.
  • Deep foundation in modern full-stack web architectures, databases, API design, microservices, and core web protocols (REST, JSON, OAuth, SSL).
  • Highly adaptable and skilled at managing multiple time-constrained priorities simultaneously with minimal guidance.

ABOUT SINCH

At Sinch we “Dream Big”, “Win Together”, “Keep it simple”, and “Make it Happen”. These values are our foundation!

DESCRIPTION

At Sinch, we put our customers at the center of everything we do. As Senior Director of Customer Success for Strategic Accounts, you will own the success, retention, and growth of Sinch's largest customer relationships. This leadership role carries accountability for net revenue retention, expansion, and executive-level advocacy across a portfolio of strategic accounts, delivering outcomes that fuel business growth and deepen partnerships at scale.

You will lead a team of Customer Success leaders and Strategic CSMs, report to the SVP of Customer Success, and collaborate closely with senior leaders in Sales, Product, Customer Excellence, and Marketing to deliver an exceptional, unified experience for our largest customers from onboarding through expansion.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead and develop a team of Customer Success Directors and Strategic CSMs responsible for Sinch's highest-value accounts. Own net revenue retention targets for the Strategic Accounts portfolio.

  • Deploy a high-touch lifecycle model for strategic accounts covering onboarding, adoption, value realization, advocacy, renewal, and expansion with tailored playbooks for complex, multi-product, multi-region customers.

  • Support the resolution of high-priority customer escalations quickly and effectively, following the lead of Customer Excellence and collaborating with Product, and executive leadership.

  • Shape deal strategy, contract renewals, and commercial expansion negotiations for strategic accounts, including usage and consumption-based revenue models.

  • Channel strategic customer insights into Product and Marketing to influence roadmap priorities, and build advocacy programs that increase NPS, reference ability, and brand champions among key accounts.

  • Build a high-performance culture by recruiting, coaching, and retaining top talent, and by creating clear career paths for strategic CS professionals.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Experience building and managing executive-level relationships with enterprise customers, including C-level engagement and complex escalation management.

  • Strategic planning and execution expertise, including multi-year account planning across global segments and verticals.

  • Experience leading and scaling teams of managers and individual contributors, with strong coaching and talent development skills.

  • Strong commercial acumen, including experience partnering with Sales on renewals, expansion, and contract negotiations.

  • Proficiency in CS and CRM platforms, reporting, automation, and data analytics tools.

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration with senior leaders across Sales, Product, Support, Marketing, and Finance.

  • Outstanding executive presence, storytelling ability, and customer advocacy experience.

  • Track record of leading change management and organizational improvement.

  • Experience in CPaaS, communications, SaaS, or usage-based business models preferred.

  • Bachelor's degree required; MBA or equivalent preferred.

OUR HIRING PROCESS

We are committed to ensuring a recruitment process that is fair, objective, consistent, and inclusive. Our approach includes structured, competency-based interviews designed to evaluate your skills, experience, and qualifications relevant to the role. At times, we may include a data-driven assessment to enhance our hiring success and identify candidates likely to excel.

We believe in a two-way process and encourage you to ask questions throughout the journey. If this role isn't what you're looking for, please explore the other opportunities listed on our career page: No matter who you are, we hope you find an exciting path forward - hopefully with us!

Benefits

  • STAY HEALTHY: We offer comprehensive market competitive medical, dental, and vision plans. A variety of supplemental plans are also provided to meet your individual needs including access to telehealth for all participants.

  • CARE FOR YOURSELF: Take advantage of our free virtual counselling resources through our global Employee Assistance Program. Your mental health is as important as your physical health.

  • SECURE YOUR FUTURE: Plan for your future with our Roth and Pre-tax 401(k) options including an employer match for all participants.

  • TAKE A BREAK: Enjoy a generous paid time off program. We value balance and understand that performance at work requires time to rest at home and/or rejuvenate on vacation.

  • PUT FAMILY FIRST: We know that families can be built in a variety of ways; therefore, we offer paid parental leave and family planning support.

  • WORK WHEREVER: Our flexible remote work offerings allow you to work wherever you are the most productive and successful. It is what you do, not where you work, that matters.

  • MAKE AN IMPACT: Support betterment in your community and beyond by taking paid time off to support a volunteer program of your choice.

  • TREAT YOURSELF: We offer discounts on retail, entertainment and more through our Reward+ program.

The estimated total annual on-target earnings (OTE) for this role are $221,000 - $276,250. The annual starting base salary for this position is $176,800 - $221,000. Factors that may affect starting pay within this range include geography/market, skills, education, experience, and other qualifications. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible to participate in the Company’s commission plan, with a target commission opportunity equal to 25% of annualized base salary, subject to the terms of the applicable commission plan.

This role will be accepting applications until October 21, 2026 at a minimum. Please note that the application timeline may be flexible to accommodate a comprehensive candidate evaluation process.

jobs.excerpt: Join Cognizant's Workday Student Practice in Australia and New Zealand and help universities transform how they manage the student journey, from first enquiry through to completion.
jobs.description:
Join Cognizant's Workday Student Practice in Australia and New Zealand and help universities transform how they manage the student journey, from first enquiry through to completion. As a Principal Consultant, you'll lead design and configuration across Student Records, including academic structure, enrolment, progression, completion and government reporting, and extend that expertise into Recruiting and Admissions, including prospect management, applications, Tertiary Admissions Centre processes and offers. You'll guide institutions on how Workday Student can best meet their needs and support their strategic goals, lead workstreams and mentor other consultants. This is a real opportunity to grow your career while helping shape how the sector operates.

This role suits a senior practitioner with a background in student records, student administration, admissions or student systems who wants to turn their knowledge of student lifecycle regulations and processes, and their commitment to supporting students, into a consulting career. You'll bring higher education and regulatory expertise to every engagement, working closely with student administration, admissions, future students, international and technology teams. You'll be equally comfortable in functional design sessions and integration discussions, making sure your designs align with Student Financials, Academic Advising, external systems and other areas of the Workday platform.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead discovery and design sessions for academic structure, student records, enrolment, unit and course changes, progression, leave of absence, withdrawal, completion and graduation.
  • Lead Admissions design across Tertiary Admissions Centre (TAC) and direct entry channels, including the pathway and alternative entry routes used by international students, transfer and non-traditional applicants, covering application processing, assessment, offers, acceptances and deferrals.
  • Configure Student Records and Admissions business processes, rules, eligibility, holds and statuses.
  • Design the end-to-end handling of Tertiary Admissions Centre (TAC) applications, preferences, offer rounds and responses, and align and collaborate with integrations and technical teams on the full solution.
  • Work with client teams to define how regional CRMs used for student recruitment interact with Workday Student, including the hand-off of prospect and applicant data.
  • Define requirements that bridge functional design and integrations, including data mapping, triggers, timing, error handling and ownership, and work closely with integration teams through build and testing.
  • Bring an understanding of how Australian or New Zealand universities manage student records to design discussions, so Workday Student is configured for local course structures, terminology, policy settings and reporting obligations.
  • Ensure designs capture the data and processes needed for TCSI reporting, Unique Student Identifier (USI) requirements, international student obligations including PRISMS and Confirmations of Enrolment, and related compliance needs.
  • Work with Student Financials and finance stakeholders to align the financial impacts of admission, enrolment, changes, withdrawal and completion events.
  • Identify data, security, privacy, records management and reporting requirements across the student lifecycle.
  • Document requirements, design decisions and configuration.
  • Prepare and execute unit testing, support end to end and integration testing and assist with defect resolution.
  • Support data conversion of historical student records, cutover preparation, training and go live readiness.
  • Provide clear advice on Workday leading practices while recognising institutional context and policy obligations.
  • Lead workstreams, coach and review the work of other consultants, and act as a trusted advisor to client process owners.
  • Contribute reusable configuration guidance, test assets and delivery methods to the Cognizant Student Practice.

Experience we are looking for

  • Senior experience in student records, student administration, admissions, student systems or a related higher education function.
  • Understanding of academic structure, enrolment, progression, completion and graduation processes, and how they are reflected in student records.
  • Familiarity with Tertiary Admissions Centre processes, such as those run by UAC, VTAC, QTAC, SATAC or TISC, including application preferences, offer rounds and data exchange with institutions.
  • Familiarity with CRMs commonly used for student recruitment in the region, such as Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics 365, and how they connect to a student information system.
  • Working knowledge of TCSI reporting, including how student, course and enrolment data is captured, validated and corrected.
  • Familiarity with the regulations that relate to student records in Australia or New Zealand, such as the Higher Education Support Act, the ESOS Act and National Code, the Higher Education Standards Framework, USI requirements, privacy and state records legislation, or the Education and Training Act and Single Data Return.
  • Ability to work with requirements that bridge functional and integration design, and to communicate confidently with both business and technical teams.
  • Proven experience guiding business stakeholders through key operational and policy decisions, including presenting options, explaining trade-offs and securing agreement.
  • Experience implementing, supporting or serving as a super-user for student information systems (SIS), with Workday Student experience highly regarded.
  • Experience leading a workstream or team and mentoring other consultants or practitioners.
  • Experience facilitating workshops, documenting decisions and working across student administration, admissions, international and technology teams preferred.
  • Experience with testing, data conversion, training or deployment readiness activities preferred.

About the Cognizant Workday Student Practice

The Cognizant Workday Student Practice is focused exclusively on helping universities across Australia and New Zealand transform the way they support students, faculty and administrators throughout the student lifecycle.

What makes our practice different is the combination of higher education practitioners and Workday specialists working together. Many of our consultants have worked inside universities as academic services professionals before moving into consulting. That experience allows us to bring practical insight into the operational, regulatory and policy considerations that shape solution design.

We work with institutions to design and implement sustainable Workday Student solutions that support local regulatory requirements, align to institutional strategy and remain adaptable as university needs evolve. Our goal is not simply to deploy technology, but to help universities establish a foundation they can continue to own, operate and enhance long after implementation is complete.

Why choose Cognizant:

  • Dare to Innovate: We push boundaries and take chances to reimagine what’s possible.

jobs.excerpt: Who we areSamsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About this role:Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, Linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.

As a Senior Embedded Software Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.

We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.

Click hereto learn more about Samsara's cultural philosophy.

In this role, you will:

  • Shape the hardware, not just the code that runs on it. Sit in reviews with our electrical engineers and argue for the right SoC, amount of flash/RAM, and combination of sensors, then prove those choices out on prototypes that reach real customers in months, not years.
  • Be the first person to make a new board do anything at all. Bring up new platforms and prototypes from virgin silicon: configure I/O, get SPI, I2C, UART, BLE talking, debug system init, validate the design, and turn unproven hardware into a product.
  • Own the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.
  • Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.
  • Work with the people who ship the whole product. Partner with product, full-stack, mobile and quality engineers so the data your firmware produces arrives intact and useful as it lands in the hands of dispatchers, fleet managers, and technicians who depend on it every shift.
  • Raise the bar for the engineers around you. At the Senior level, you are a force multiplier for your team. Through thoughtful designs, rigorous reviews, hands-on mentorship, and sound technical judgment, you help other engineers deliver better work. You lead by example, strengthen engineering practices, and connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes. You bring clarity to ambiguous problems, act with intellectual honesty and urgency, and deliver high-quality solutions iteratively.

What you bring

  • 8+ years building firmware for resource-constrained systems, You have delivered reliable firmware where memory, processing power, energy and timing are all scarce, and you know how to measure, optimize and make deliberate trade-offs between them.
  • You have led firmware development for several new products end to end. You have taken firmware from initial concept through architecture, technical implementation, validation, and product launch, providing hands-on technical leadership throughout.
  • Substantial bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.
  • You have brought up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.
  • Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.
  • Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.
  • Senior-level scope. You have led work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have consistently driven consensus across teams.
  • Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you make that trade-off on purpose.
  • Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.
  • You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.
  • You ship fast without shipping badly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.
  • You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.

What will set you apart

  • BLE at depth - You understand what’s going on down the PHY and can build orchestration for the system to use in a performant and power efficient way.
  • Cellular IoT - LTE-M or NB-IoT modem integration, power state management, and the certification gauntlet (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approval).
  • Securing embedded systems end to end - secure boot, firmware signing, cryptography, and key management that survives contact with manufacturing.
  • OTA and device firmware update at fleet scale - A/B partitions, rollback, and the discipline of never bricking a device you cannot physically reach.
  • You’ve been on the factory floor - You have an understanding of the processes behind the mass production and quality assurance of electronics. You have a track record of fixing production show stoppers.

jobs.excerpt: About LyntonLynton spent 16 years as a HubSpot partner, delivering 2,000+ projects across 50+ industries.
jobs.description:
About Lynton

Lynton spent 16 years as a HubSpot partner, delivering 2,000+ projects across 50+ industries. We know SaaS and agency work from the inside. When we saw what was coming with AI, we left HubSpot to build what comes next.

We build and run AI-native growth systems for mid-market companies: websites built to be measured, an open-source stack that replaces legacy software, and AI agents that run marketing, sales, and operations. The client owns the infrastructure, we operate the agents, and the whole system has to show what it produces in revenue.

If this role sounds like a perfect fit for you, skip ahead to apply directly on our website. We prioritize candidates who apply directly on our site.

The opportunity

Most agencies have added AI to their production line and kept the creative process they had ten years ago. We started over. AI coding agents build our websites. Our imagery comes from image and video models we direct. The interactive work that used to need a studio and a six-figure budget is now something a small team can ship in weeks.

What that makes possible depends on taste. Anyone can generate a thousand images. Very few people can pick the right one, fix what's wrong with it, and make it move in a way that serves the page's argument. That's the job.

As our founding creative director, you own the creative and communication strategy for every website and campaign Lynton ships, both ours and our clients'. You decide what a page says and how it looks. You design how it moves. You make or direct every image, illustration, animation, and film on it. Some weeks you're writing the headline. Other weeks you're lighting a scene in Blender, or telling a client their brand deserves better than stock photography.

The agency is one part of what we're building. Lynton is also a launchpad for new products, services, and companies we incubate from inside, and with your help we'll take each of them to market.

What you'll own

  • Creative and communication strategy. Own the messaging and visual system for every site and campaign. That covers positioning, page structure, headlines, body copy, the design language, and the design tokens that encode it. You write copy yourself and edit everything that ships, so the words and pictures come from one point of view.
  • Interactive experience design. Design how every page moves and responds, including SVG and CSS animation, scroll-driven storytelling, micro-interactions, and real-time 3D. You storyboard it, prototype it, and direct the build. When getting into the timeline yourself is faster than explaining, you do that.
  • 3D and real-time scenes. Model, light, and art-direct scenes in Blender, then bring them to the browser with Three.js and WebGL. You set the bar for when a page earns real-time 3D and when a lighter technique tells the story better.
  • Generated photography and illustration. Build and run the image pipeline. You'll art-direct photography and illustration with image models, keep one style consistent across a whole site or campaign, and retouch what the model gets wrong. You'll also animate stills with video models. You set the house rules on style, consistency, and licensing.
  • Video and motion graphics. Produce product films, launch and explainer videos, social cuts, and motion graphics. Use generative video, compositing, and traditional motion tools in whatever mix gets the best result.
  • Campaign creative. Own launches and email campaigns end to end: concept, copy, landing pages, imagery, and video. A campaign should read as one idea from the inbox to the page.
  • New products, services, and brands. Lead the creative for every launch we incubate: the name and identity, the positioning and story, and the site and campaign it goes to market with.
  • Creative oversight on every engagement. You review and sign off on all creative the agency ships. You're the reason a Lynton site looks and reads like one, and the reason no client site looks like a template.
  • Performance and accessibility as part of the craft. We hold every page to a mobile Lighthouse score of 90 or above and to WCAG AA contrast. Motion respects reduced-motion settings. 3D loads after the headline, so it never delays the first thing a visitor reads. Copy lives in the page, where both people and AI assistants can read it.
  • AI-first production. Direct our agent fleet through the production work: coding agents for prototypes and builds, image and video models for assets, and language models for first drafts and variants. Manage each engagement's inference and render budget like any other resource. Build reusable pipelines so every project starts further ahead than the last.

Who you are

  • 8+ years in digital creative, with at least three leading it. You've been a creative director, associate CD, or design lead at an interactive studio, an agency, or an in-house brand team. You've answered for the work across many projects at once.
  • A portfolio of interactive work you directed and helped build. Your sites use motion to carry the story rather than to decorate it. Awards are nice. Work we can click through and feel is what counts.
  • You write. You can turn a positioning brief into a homepage headline and the three paragraphs under it. You can edit someone else's copy until it sounds like a person. To you, words and pictures are one job.
  • Hands-on across the motion stack. You're fluent in CSS and SVG animation, GSAP or an equivalent, and scroll-driven sequencing. You've shipped real-time 3D in the browser with Three.js, React Three Fiber, or similar, and built or lit scenes in Blender, Cinema 4D, or Houdini. You don't need to be the strongest engineer in the room, but you can read the code, prototype with a coding agent, and tell when a build is wrong.
  • Deep, current practice with image and video models. You use them every day and have opinions about which to use for what. You know how to keep a character, a product, or an illustration style consistent across dozens of outputs. You also know where the models still fail.
  • Motion and video craft. You can cut a film, design motion graphics, and finish in After Effects, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, or their equivalents, alongside generative tools.
  • Taste you can explain. You can say why a typeface, a cut, or a camera move is right, in terms a client or an engineer can act on.
  • Honest with the medium. You'd never present a generated person as a real customer. You know the commercial terms of the models you use. You'd rather ship an honest illustration than a misleading photograph.
  • Performance-minded. You've traded a heavier scene for a faster page and can explain the call. Texture budgets, draw calls, and Core Web Vitals are part of your craft vocabulary.
  • AI-first in practice. You already direct agents across design, code, and copy. You can spec a task, judge the output, and improve the loop. For you, directing agents is the appeal rather than the threat.
  • Ready to build. You're comfortable with a blank page, a small team, and a leadership group that builds alongside you.

Bonus

  • Shaders, GLSL, or generative art
  • Rive, Lottie, or Spline for lightweight interactive motion
  • Sound design for web and film
  • Brand identity systems built from scratch
  • Training or fine-tuning image models on a brand's style
  • B2B or professional-services clients

Why this role

  • Ground floor with credibility. We have 27 years in business, 16 years of enterprise relationships, and a client base that generates revenue. You'll build the creative function of a new kind of agency on a real foundation.
  • The whole creative surface. Strategy, words, design, interaction, 3D, image, and video all sit with one person. There's no handoff between a copy team, a design team, and a motion vendor.
  • The new tools are the daily workflow here. The models and agents most studios are still piloting are a budget line and an everyday habit at Lynton.
  • Direct to leadership. You work directly with the CMO and the founder, with no creative committee in between, and your work ships to real clients.

Summary

Join the Foundation in our ambitious project to empower people to create and share the sum of all human knowledge. We are looking for a Lead Financial Analyst to serve as the strategic business partner to our Product & Technology department, one of the most dynamic and fastest-growing parts of the organization, with a combined budget of more than $100M. You will also support other key areas of our work and, as the most senior analyst on the Financial Business Partner team, be responsible for driving improvements in financial planning, analytics, and our business partnership practices.

This is a business partnering role first and an FP&A role second. You will sit alongside product and engineering leaders, help them weigh investment tradeoffs before decisions are made, and turn roadmaps into financial plans. You will work directly with the Chief of Product and Technology (CPTO), the Chief Financial Officer (CFO), and the broader executive team. This is a chance to have an outsized impact on a mission-driven organization that operates one of the most visited websites in the world.

This role is remote and open to candidates between UTC-8 and UTC+1.

Why this role

  • Be the trusted finance advisor to Product & Technology leadership, with a real voice in how we invest more than $100M in people, infrastructure, and partners.
  • Work on infrastructure that serves more than 20 billion views per month.
  • Drive projects with impact and executive visibility, including our CPTO and CFO.
  • Shape the future of our business partner function by leading projects, setting standards, and mentoring other analysts.
  • Join a collaborative, globally distributed team that values knowledge sharing.

What you'll do

Be the Finance Partner to Product & Technology, and a second department

  • Act as the lead finance partner to department leaders and budget owners, providing analysis that informs prioritization and investment trade-offs.
  • Join planning and roadmap conversations early as the voice of finance, raising tradeoffs and risks before commitments are made.
  • Provide the financial voice in business strategy across our technical infrastructure and product development objectives.

Our Story

TopDog Law is not your typical law firm. We're a nationally scaling personal injury firm built for impact and growth, growing the client experience end-to-end, from marketing and intake through litigation. We believe that world-class marketing, paired with exceptional legal talent and operations, creates better experiences and outcomes for clients and the business alike.

Over the past three years, we've grown 2–3x year over year, setting a new standard on the marketing side of the personal injury space and proving what's possible when strategy, speed, and execution align. Now we're applying that same discipline and innovation to firm operations, case management, and national scale, intentionally building the infrastructure, systems, and teams to grow without sacrificing quality, culture, or accountability.

We are a fully remote team that share trust, open communication, and a commitment to doing great work. If you love ownership, thrive in a fast-moving environment, and want to help build something exceptional, you'll feel right at home here.

The Opportunity

We need litigation attorneys who know how to issue spot, problem solve, and think creatively to best serve our clients. Our top performers are organized, strategic thinkers, and passionate about helping regular people maximize the value of their cases. We challenge insurance companies to be fair with our injured clients.

What You Will Own

  • Own the client communication;
  • Identify the appropriate deadlines and meet them;
  • Build the case from start to finish;
  • Identify creative solutions with strategic legal thinking; and
  • Partner with other team members to best serve our clients needs.

What You Bring

Required:

  • Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree from an accredited law school
  • Active admission to the Georgia Bar
  • 5 - 10 years of experience in Personal Injury law
  • Strong communication, negotiation, research, and writing skills
  • Ability to manage a robust case load independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment
  • Knowledge of Georgia laws, regulations, and procedures required
  • Must be located in or near the State of Georgia
  • Strong communication skills—written and verbal
  • Ability to think critically, prioritize effectively, and execute with speed

Preferred (Nice to Have):

  • Active Admission to one or more districts of Georgia Federal Court

Who Thrives Here (Core Values)

We don't hire on resumes alone. We hire for competence, character, and mindset.

  • Embrace Change: Open to feedback, embracing change, and always asking "what's next?"

We’re a global, midsize CRO that pushes boundaries, innovates and invents because the path to a cure for the world’s most persistent diseases is not paved by those who play it safe. It is built by those who take pioneering, creative approaches and implement them with quality and excellence.
